_meta.//: SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR EVERY OTHER LANGUAGE. Every key that exists here must exist in every other file in this directory, with the same placeholders in it - scripts/i18nprobe.ts fails the build otherwise. The English values are also load-bearing in another way: forty browser harnesses select elements by their visible text, so changing a string here is changing a test selector.
_meta.name: English

selection.rotBalancedDesc: Tired first-choice players sit out the lower-ranked competitions.

tactics.sliderStyleUp: Wider attack: better attack, weaker scrum and breakdown.
tactics.sliderStyleDown: Forward-led: stronger scrum and maul, fewer chances out wide.
tactics.sliderTempoUp: Faster: better attack, but players tire faster and the defence is looser.
tactics.sliderTempoDown: Slower: players tire less and the defence holds shape, but the attack is weaker.
tactics.sliderKickingUp: Kick more: your kickers matter more and it helps in bad weather. Attack and breakdown are weaker.
tactics.sliderKickingDown: Kick less: better attack and breakdown, but mistakes happen in your own half.
tactics.sliderAggressionUp: More aggressive: stronger breakdown, but more penalties and yellow cards. A strict referee punishes this more.
tactics.sliderAggressionDown: More disciplined: fewer penalties and cards, weaker breakdown. Best against a strict referee.
tactics.sliderDefLineUp: Faster line speed: better defence and more turnovers, more offside penalties and cards.
tactics.sliderDefLineDown: Slower line speed: fewer penalties, but their attack gets more time.
tactics.sliderDefWidthUp: Wide defence: stops wide attacks, weaker against forwards through the middle.
tactics.sliderDefWidthDown: Narrow defence: stops forward-led attacks, weaker out wide.
tactics.presetAlloutDesc: Wide and fast. For chasing a score.
tactics.presetShutupDesc: Slow the game, keep shape and kick for territory. For protecting a lead.
tactics.presetCornersDesc: Kick for territory and pressure their exits.
tactics.styleBalancedDesc: No fixed style. Adjust each week.
tactics.styleHightempoDesc: Fast pace. Needs a fit squad.
tactics.styleOffloadDesc: Offloads in contact. More chances, more errors.
tactics.defSitBackDesc: Deep line. Fewest penalties, most metres conceded.
tactics.defDriftDesc: Slide towards the touchline. Good against wide attacks, weak through the middle.
tactics.defStandardDesc: Even line and speed. No strength, no weakness.
tactics.defManDesc: Narrow, one-on-one. Good against forwards, weak out wide.
tactics.defPressDesc: Fast rush. The strongest defence, and the most offside penalties.
tactics.z22LongDesc: Kick long. Most ground gained, possession lost.
tactics.z22BoxDesc: Box kick and compete for it. The usual choice.
tactics.z22PlayDesc: Run it from your own 22. High reward, high risk.
tactics.zMidTerrDesc: Kick for the corners. Fewer chances, closer to their line.
tactics.zMidBalancedDesc: Kick or run as the play allows.
tactics.zMidHandDesc: Run through the middle. More chances, further from their line.
tactics.zOppDriveDesc: Forwards carry close to the ruck. Wins penalties as well as tries.
tactics.zOppSpreadDesc: Move it wide. The most tries, and the most errors.
tactics.zOppPatientDesc: Build phases. Fewer tries and fewer errors than the other two.
tactics.sliderCommitUp: More players at each ruck: safer ball, fewer attackers.
tactics.sliderCommitDown: Fewer players at each ruck: more attackers and faster ball, more turnovers conceded.
tactics.sliderContestUp: Contest their rucks: more turnovers, thinner defence, more penalties.
tactics.sliderContestDown: Leave their rucks: a fuller defensive line, but they get fast ball.

roles.linkDesc: Attack and breakdown up, scrum down.
roles.aerialDesc: Defence and kicking up, attack down.

playbook.lo_frontDesc: Short throw to the front. Rarely lost, rarely leads to a chance.
playbook.lo_middleDesc: Standard throw to the middle. No strength, no weakness.
playbook.lo_backDesc: Long throw to the back. Better attacking ball, but more likely to be stolen.
playbook.lo_dummyDesc: Fake to the front, throw to the back. Hard for them to read, slow for you to master.
playbook.lo_maulDesc: Catch and drive a maul. The strongest attacking lineout, and the slowest ball.
playbook.lo_topDesc: Ball tapped straight down to the 9. Fast ball, but no maul to drive.
playbook.sc_channel1Desc: Ball out quickly past the hooker. Fast ball, less push.
playbook.sc_holdDesc: Hold the ball at the No. 8's feet. A stable platform.
playbook.sc_shoveDesc: Push hard for a penalty. Wins penalties if your pack is stronger, concedes them if it is not.
playbook.sc_wheelDesc: Turn the scrum and attack off the side. Needs a technically strong pack.

armsrace.tapeSet: Their analysts have your {move_k} on {pct}% of your first-phase ball, and this coach sets the defence for what the tape shows.
armsrace.tapeCalm: Their analysts have your {move_k} on {pct}% of your first-phase ball, but this coach does not change much for it.
armsrace.tapeUnread: Their analysts have your {move_k} on {pct}% of your first-phase ball. Whether they will set up for it, the report cannot say.

moves.mv_1331Desc: A pod of three forwards either side of the ruck and a forward on each edge. Carries across the whole width.
moves.mv_242Desc: Four forwards in midfield and two back-rowers out on each edge, running at the backs.
moves.mv_backdoorDesc: Three forwards off the 9 as a pod, with the 10 hidden behind them for the pass out the back.
moves.mv_crashDesc: The 12 runs a hard, straight line off the 10 and takes the contact. Simple, safe, and over the gain line.
moves.mv_switchDesc: The 10 runs across the field and the 13 cuts back behind on a scissors. Wrong-foots a drifting line.
moves.mv_loopDesc: The 10 misses the 12, loops round the back and takes it again outside. Makes an extra man.
moves.mv_decoyDesc: The 12 runs a hard decoy line and the 10 passes out the back of it to the 13 or the 15.
moves.mv_blindDesc: Off the scrum the 8 picks up, the 9 goes blind and the 11 wraps round on the outside.
moves.mv_insideDesc: The 10 drifts across the defence and pops the ball back inside to the 12 on a late line.
moves.mv_strike13Desc: Lineout strike: the 12 takes it flat and the 13 hits a short line through the midfield gap.
moves.mv_winginDesc: The blind wing leaves his touchline and hits the 10-12 channel at pace off a flat 10, with the 12 as the decoy. The man nobody counted.
moves.mv_widthDesc: Short flat passes along the line and the 15 into it from depth, then the ball on to the far touch. Width off first phase.
moves.mv_peelDesc: The maul sets, the hooker takes it off the back and runs across it, and the blind wing cuts in on his shoulder.
moves.mv_maulswitchDesc: Red zone only. The lineout splits into two pods; they compete at one, the ball goes to the other, and it binds and drives for the line.
moves.mv_tapDesc: Penalty slot only. The 9 taps, one pod shapes to drive, and the ball goes to the second pod and round its corner.
moves.mv_tapspreadDesc: Penalty slot only. The 9 taps, the forwards run hard flat lines at the mark, and the ball goes out the back of them to the 10 and along the line.
moves.mv_tapgoDesc: Penalty slot only. The 9 taps and pops to a forward on a hard line off the mark, two more bind on him, and they drive on.
moves.mv_crashswingDesc: Two phases: a flat crash ball with a back-rower on the shoulder, then off the quick ruck the ball goes back the other way to the far edge.
moves.mv_loop9Desc: The 10 runs straight at the fringe and the 9, who followed his pass round the back, takes the tip outside him.
moves.mv_crosskickDesc: A flat line draws them up and the 10 puts the ball on the far wing, running onto it.
moves.mv_grubberDesc: Against a line rushing up, the 10 rolls it through between two defenders for the centres to chase.
moves.heading: Playbook
moves.headingSub: set moves you call and drill
moves.mixLabel: Primary strike on {pct}% of the ball both can run off
moves.slotHint: Tap a slot to put it there.
moves.tapHint: Tap a move to see it run.

bench.split53Desc: 5 forwards and 3 backs. Cover for every position.
bench.split62Desc: 6 forwards and 2 backs. Stronger up front late on; a back injury may put a forward in the backline.
bench.split44Desc: 4 forwards and 4 backs. Fresh legs and cover out wide; less push late on.
bench.briefOrdersDesc: Plays the same job as the player replaced.
bench.briefImpactDesc: More carrying, less defending. Tires quickly.
bench.briefShoreDesc: Tackles and discipline. Fewer risks in attack.
bench.briefManageDesc: Kicks for territory to keep play in their half.

analyst.noMatchToStudy: No match this week, so nothing to study. He will have a read on the next opponent as soon as one is in the diary.
analyst.noReadsYet: No reads followed yet this era.
analyst.followedReads: Followed {n} of his reads: right {right}, wrong {wrong}.
analyst.sureStake: I would stake my job on this
analyst.sureHunch: It is a hunch, but a decent one
analyst.andTest: , and {name} is the one to test
analyst.weakScrum: their scrum goes backwards under pressure
analyst.weakLineout: their lineout is a lottery beyond the front pod
analyst.weakDefence: their defensive line comes up in ones and twos
analyst.weakAttack: they have no shape once the first phase breaks down
analyst.weakKicking: their kicking game hands territory back every time
analyst.howScrum: Live scrummaging all week. Squeeze them and the penalties come.
analyst.howLineout: Set-piece work: contest their throw and the platform collapses.
analyst.howDefence: Attacking shapes. Move them side to side and holes appear.
analyst.howKicking: Attacking shapes and quick counters off their loose kicks.
analyst.howAttack: Defensive drills. Squeeze the space and let them run out of ideas.
analyst.noMatchToStudy_w: No match this week, so nothing to study. She will have a read on the next opponent as soon as one is in the diary.
analyst.followedReads_w: Followed {n} of her reads: right {right}, wrong {wrong}.

forms.runningSubj: {club} are playing with the handbrake off
forms.running: The ball is going through the hands at {club}. Supporters have started calling it running rugby, and quick backs around the league have noticed.
forms.kickingSubj: {club} are winning it with the boot
forms.kicking: Territory, pressure and a kicking game the rest of the league has learned to expect. Kickers and good decision makers want to play in a side like this.
forms.pack: Set piece, maul, carry, repeat. {club} are becoming a forwards' club, and big forwards across the league are taking an interest.
forms.flair: The quality at {club} is out wide, and the rugby shows it. Back-line flair is becoming what the club is known for.
forms.academy: More and more of the minutes at {club} are going to players they brought through themselves. Young players are listening, the academy coaches are sending up better classes, and the terraces are proud of it. They will also notice if a big cheque ever pushes one of their own out.
forms.spenders: {club} are buying rather than building, and the market knows it. Players who follow the money are ringing first.
forms.prudent: Money in the bank and the books going the right way. Sponsors like it, and so do players who plan a career. The board will expect it to stay that way.
forms.stretched: The balance at {club} is heading the wrong way, and people have started to say so. The board will be watching the accounts closely.

identity.fades: '{label_k}' no longer describes {club} the way it did. The club is turning into something else.
identity.fansObjectSubj: The terraces question a big signing
identity.fansObject: {club} built a name on bringing their own through, and some supporters are unhappy that {player} has arrived for a big fee in the shirt {own} has been wearing. {own} is said to be quietly disappointed.
identity.academyKept: Homegrown regulars at {club} this season: {n}. The supporters see the club keeping its word, and the mood on the terraces is better for it.
identity.academyStalled: {club} are meant to be an academy club, but not one homegrown player held down a place this season. The supporters have noticed, and so has the board.
identity.prudenceBroken: {club} had earned a name for careful money, and this season the balance fell a long way. The board has made it clear that is not what it signed up for.
identity.stretchedMending: After a spell of living beyond their means, {club} have put money back into the account this season. The board has noticed, and is pleased.

oppreport.title: Opposition report: {club}
oppreport.bandHint_vague: Little tape and a small analysis suite. Treat these as rough guides.
oppreport.bandHint_fair: A decent read, with some guesswork at the edges.
oppreport.bandHint_sharp: Plenty of tape and a good suite. Still not gospel.
oppreport.formNone: No competitive results on tape yet.

form.other: Last {n}: {w}W {d}D {l}L, scoring {pf} and conceding {pa} a game.

oppreport.styleUnclear: Their shape is hard to pin down from the tape we have.
oppreport.dial_style_lo: They keep it tight through the forwards (style reads {lo} to {hi}).
oppreport.dial_tempo_hi: They play at pace (tempo reads {lo} to {hi}).
oppreport.dial_tempo_lo: They slow the game down (tempo reads {lo} to {hi}).
oppreport.dial_kicking_hi: They kick a lot (kicking reads {lo} to {hi}).
oppreport.dial_kicking_lo: They keep ball in hand (kicking reads {lo} to {hi}).
oppreport.dial_aggression_hi: They are abrasive in contact (physicality reads {lo} to {hi}).
oppreport.dial_aggression_lo: They play a clean game (physicality reads {lo} to {hi}).
oppreport.dial_defLine_hi: Their line rushes up (line speed reads {lo} to {hi}).
oppreport.dial_defLine_lo: Their line sits back and drifts (line speed reads {lo} to {hi}).
oppreport.spNoFootage: Not enough footage to call their set-piece habits.
oppreport.spCalls: Set piece: lineouts mostly {lo}, scrums mostly {sc}.
oppreport.spPredictable: They call the same moves week after week. Their set piece can be read.
oppreport.coach_stubborn: Their dugout plays its own game whoever is in front of it.
oppreport.coach_analyst: Their dugout studies our recent matches and sets up against our habits.
oppreport.coach_reactive: Their dugout changes things from the touchline once the match is on.
oppreport.readingYou: They have been reading our tape: expect them to lean towards the counter to our usual plan.
oppreport.coachUnknown: We cannot yet tell how their dugout adapts.
oppreport.respect: They rate us: expect a cautious, spoiling game.
oppreport.respectUnit: They rate us, and they will go after our {unit}.
oppreport.lastMetW: Last time we met we won {us}-{them}.
oppreport.lastMetL: Last time we met we lost {us}-{them}.
oppreport.lastMetD: Last time we met it finished {us}-{them}.
oppreport.recallWeak: Their {unit} struggled: we won {pct}% of that contest.
oppreport.recallStrong: Their {unit} had the better of us: we won only {pct}% of that contest.
oppreport.lastPlan_failed: Our plan then ({plan}) did not come off.
oppreport.planDesc_lesson: Back at their {unit}, which struggled last time.
oppreport.planDesc_counter: The assistant's answer to how they play.
oppreport.planDesc_finish: Legs for the last twenty, and a bench told to hit hard.
oppreport.planDesc_starve: Keep it in hand, slow it down and win every ruck, so their back three hardly see it.
oppreport.planSub: Each plan only sets controls you already have. Change them afterwards and the plan is off.
oppreport.testNote: A Test week: the union's camp runs the preparation, so this report is for reading. The club's dials and calls stay at the club.
oppreport.filed: Filed for the next time we meet them.

find.ballNoPoints: We had {poss}% of the ball and could not turn it into tries.
find.wonWithout: We won on {poss}% possession: the defence did the work.
find.starved: Only {poss}% of the ball. They kept it away from us.
find.clinical: Clinical: {n} tries from {poss}% of the ball.
find.lateFade: We faded: they scored {n} points in the last twenty.
find.lateStrong: We finished the stronger: {n} points in the last twenty.
find.missedTackles: {n} missed tackles, {pct}% of our attempts. Too many.
find.fresher: We finished fresher: {mine}% in the tank against their {theirs}%.
find.tired: We ran out of legs: {mine}% in the tank against their {theirs}%.
find.spWon: Our {unit} was on top: {pct}% of the contest.
find.spLost: Our {unit} was beaten: {pct}% of the contest.
find.spEven: The set piece was even. Nobody got a platform from it.
find.playerBoth: Standout: {best} ({r}). A day to forget for {worst} ({r2}).
find.planDropped: The plan ({plan}) was set but not carried through, so it cannot be judged.
find.plan_worked: The plan ({plan}) worked: the target was hit and so was the result.
find.plan_partly: The plan ({plan}) half worked: the target or the result, not both.
find.plan_failed: The plan ({plan}) did not come off.
find.testWeek: A Test week: the camp's preparation, not a club plan.
find.noPlan: No plan was set for this one. We played it off the cuff.

philosophy.packBlurb: Forward-led: mauls from lineouts, pick-and-go, pressure at the scrum.
philosophy.packSoft: Weak if their forwards get slow ball.
philosophy.widthBlurb: Moves the ball wide early and offloads in contact.
philosophy.widthSoft: Weak if you win the collisions and force handling errors.
philosophy.tempoBlurb: Quick taps and fast rucks to tire you out.
philosophy.tempoSoft: Weak if you keep your defensive shape; they tire late on.
philosophy.squeezeBlurb: Kicks for territory and puts pressure on your exits.
philosophy.squeezeSoft: Weak against strong counter-attack from their kicks.
philosophy.blitzBlurb: Fast rush defence, then kicks turnovers long.
philosophy.blitzSoft: Weak to kicks and passes behind the rush.
philosophy.counterSoft: Weak if you keep the ball through the phases.
philosophy.chaosBlurb: Fast, physical and loose. Strong in broken play.
philosophy.chaosSoft: Weak against a disciplined side: they concede penalties.
philosophy.structureBlurb: Set plays and patient phases. Few penalties conceded.
philosophy.structureSoft: Weak when rushed into unplanned play.
philosophy.counter_pack: Match them up front. Do not go wide off slow ball.
philosophy.counter_width: Kick for territory so they have to attack from deep.
philosophy.counter_squeeze: Run their kicks back at them.
philosophy.counter_blitz: Attack around the rush, not into it, and keep penalties down.
philosophy.counter_counter: Keep the ball. Kick only when your chase is ready.
philosophy.counter_chaos: Stay disciplined and let them give penalties away.
philosophy.counter_structure: Put them under pressure early with line speed.

matchday.adviceCard: {player} is walking a tightrope - one more infringement and it's red.
matchday.advicePoor: {player} is having one of those days ({rating}) - fresh legs might spare him.
matchday.anthems: Anthems done, jerseys presented. Substitutions and the team talk are yours from the touchline.
matchday.badBloodRest: . Expect cards, a hostile atmosphere and a contest the form book can't call.
matchday.frNoneNote: Nobody on the bench is trained for the front row. Anyone can go on, but the scrums may go uncontested.
matchday.frOnlyNote: A front-row shirt: while there is a trained front-rower on the bench, only a front-rower can take it.
matchday.injNoCover: Nobody is left on the bench, so the side plays on a player short. Close this to carry on.
matchday.injUncontested: Scrums are uncontested from here: nobody left is trained for the front row.
matchday.bogeyRest: - you have never beaten them, and the players know it. End it today.
matchday.breakTitle: 60' - a break in play, final quarter ahead
matchday.brinkApps: makes career appearance number {n} if he takes the field
matchday.brinkLine: ({pos}) {what}. The ground will know the moment it happens.

brinkPts.one: needs {n} point to reach {mark} in his career
brinkPts.other: needs {n} points to reach {mark} in his career

matchday.brinkTry: is one try away from {n} in his career, and he is in the form to get it
matchday.callFirst: The touchline call is yours first
matchday.crisisNote: A full-blown crisis: the squad cannot field fifteen fit men. The assistant will patch the gaps with whoever can stand.
matchday.dangerBody: ({pos}) is the one to shackle - {club} play through him. Keep him quiet and you're halfway there.
matchday.derbyBody: The form book goes in the bin, the cards come out, and the town keeps the score longer than the league table does.
matchday.derbyFirst: Your first one. Win it and they will sing your name; lose it and they will remember that too.
matchday.farewellAway: This is your last trip to face him on his own patch. Great players deserve a great send-off. Just not the winning kind.
matchday.farewellHome: This is the final time {club} bring him to your ground. Beat him, then applaud him off.
matchday.farewellPre: ({age}, {pos}) has announced this season is his last.
matchday.finalBody: Eighty minutes from the {comp}. Everything the season has been builds to this - there is no next week, no second leg, no points for a brave defeat. Win it.
matchday.finishersNone: Every replacement is simply covering a shirt. No special instructions.
matchday.fixItNote: The team cannot kick off as it is. Fix It lets the assistant repair the team sheet and start the match. Not Yet goes back so you can sort it yourself.
matchday.happyRest: - they have never beaten you. Keep it that way.

matchday.hintFree: The assistant has sent {player} on. Tap someone else to change it, free of charge, or tap him again to keep him.
matchday.hintNoneLeft: No tactical replacements left. You can still tap two men on the pitch to swap their positions.
matchday.hintTap: Tap a man on the pitch, then tap who comes on for him. Tapping a second man on the pitch swaps their positions instead.
matchday.howWatch: How will you watch this one?
matchday.injNote: Name his replacement before play restarts.
matchday.intlLine: International rugby - the whole country is watching, coach.
matchday.msTry: try number {n} of his career would bring up {mark}
matchday.mustDecide: Play is stopped until somebody takes his shirt. Tap the man you want on, or tap the assistant's pick again to keep him.
matchday.noScores: No scores yet. Somebody has to blink first.
matchday.oldBoyOurs: ({pos}) returns to a former home - {n} appearances for {club}. He knows their calls.
matchday.oldBoyTheirs: ({pos}) faces the club he left - {n} appearances in your colours. Expect him to play like it is a final.
matchday.optCornerD: Lineout five metres out. Maul for the try - glory or nothing.
matchday.optPostsDLead: {kicker} lines it up. Safe three - levels or leads.
matchday.optTapD: Catch them flat-footed. Keeps the tempo scorching.
matchday.pausedTitle: Play is paused - change the picture
matchday.penCall: Penalty - your call from the touchline
matchday.planAir1: You own the air. Kick for touch and strangle the field position.
matchday.planAir2: Their lineout wobbles under pressure. Kick to the corners and feast on the throw.
matchday.planApply: Apply the plan - adjust my tactics
matchday.planHeated1: This one will boil over. Be the calmer side and let them implode.
matchday.planHeated2: Bad blood in this fixture. Let them throw the punches and take the points from the penalties.
matchday.planLenient1: {ref} lets it flow - lift the tempo and fight every breakdown.
matchday.planLenient2: {ref} keeps the whistle in his pocket. The breakdown is a street fight today - win it.
matchday.planScrumThem1: Avoid the arm wrestle - their pack is a handful. Play away from the set-piece.
matchday.planScrumThem2: Do not feed their scrum. Quick taps, quick lineouts, keep the big lads honest and blowing.
matchday.planScrumThem3: Their pack wants a fight we cannot win. Deny them the set-piece and stretch the game.
matchday.planScrumUs1: Their scrum creaks. Keep it tight and squeeze the penalties out of them.
matchday.planScrumUs2: We have them at the scrum. March them backwards until the referee gets bored of whistling.
matchday.planScrumUs3: Their front row is the weak link. Every scrum is three points waiting to happen.
matchday.planStrict1: {ref} cards early - discipline first at the ruck.
matchday.planStrict2: {ref} referees the letter of the law. Stay on your feet, hands off, no cheap shots.
matchday.planTired1: Their legs are heavy this week. Run them off their feet.
matchday.planTired2: They backed up a hard match and it shows. High tempo from the first whistle and they will crack late.
matchday.planWet1: {weather} forecast - put boot to ball and pin the corners. Handling sides drown in this.
matchday.planWet2: {weather} on the way. Territory wins this one: kick long, chase hard, let them make the mistakes.
matchday.planWet3: Filthy weather due. Keep the ball off the deck at your peril - this is a day for the boot and the maul.
matchday.planWide1: Their edge defence is the soft spot. Go wide and shift the point of attack.
matchday.planWide2: Numbers out wide win this. Two passes past the ruck and they are scrambling.
matchday.planWide3: Their wings tuck in. Earn the corner and the tries will follow.
matchday.prepAttack: Attacking Shapes - strike moves drilled all week. Attack sharpened.
matchday.prepDefence: Defensive Drills - the wall is built. Defence sharpened.
matchday.prepFitness: Conditioning - the legs will last longer than theirs.
matchday.prepRecovery: Recovery Week - fresh bodies, full tanks.
matchday.prepSetpiece: Set-Piece Work - scrum and lineout honed to a point.
matchday.quote1: We know exactly how they want to play - and we're ready for it.
matchday.quote2: No excuses from us this week. We've targeted this one.
matchday.quote3: They're a good side, but this is our patch.
matchday.quote4: People keep writing us off. Suits us fine.
matchday.quote5: We've had a good week. You'll see a response on Saturday.
matchday.readyOk: Everything looks in order. The tunnel awaits.
matchday.readyTitle: Are you ready for the game?
matchday.refFlow: Plays advantage and lets it flow.
matchday.refFussy: Fussy at the tackle - hands off, or it is a penalty.
matchday.refJackal: Lets the jackal work - a strong breakdown will win turnovers.
matchday.refNothing: Nothing marked in his book: he lets the players decide it.
matchday.refCrowd: A big home crowd: the tight calls may lean {team}'s way.
matchday.refPatient: Patient: he allows {n} before reaching for a card.
matchday.refScrumLoose: Waves the scrum away - your set piece is worth less today.
matchday.refScrumTight: Pedantic at the scrum - the dominant front row gets rewarded.
matchday.refShortFuse: Short fuse: {n} penalties and somebody walks.
matchday.stillGoing: Your match against {opp} is still going. It carries on exactly where you left it.
matchday.stillOver: Your match against {opp} has reached full time. The result stands.

rotButton.one: Rotate the XV - rest the flagged man
rotButton.other: Rotate the XV - rest the flagged men

matchday.rotCup: A cup tie is the week to trust the squad.
matchday.rotFlagged: {men} - {count} flagged by the medical staff. Say the word and I'll name a fresh XV around them.
matchday.rotSummary: The medical staff have flagged {n} of the intended XV - tired legs or too many minutes. Say the word and I'll name a fresh XV around them.
matchday.rotTurnaround: A {n}-day turnaround is no week for heavy legs.

skipTook.one: Skip answered {n} touchline call for you - the points were taken.
skipTook.other: Skip answered {n} touchline calls for you - the points were taken.

matchday.spCalmD: Settles everyone a little. Rarely wrong, rarely a masterstroke.
matchday.spExpectD: Raises the stakes. Cures complacency; crushes a nervous room.
matchday.spFaithD: Lifts belief. Right for a room short of it, wrong for one with too much.
matchday.spFireD: The biggest lift. Wakes a flat side; tips a cocky one into indiscipline.
matchday.spdFastName: Fast - a skim for the incidents
matchday.stakesBottomTwo: You are in the bottom two. Every point is survival.
matchday.stakesClimb: A win is worth at least four: close enough to climb today.
matchday.stakesKnockout: Knockout rugby. Win and the {comp} run goes on; lose and it ends this afternoon.

stakesPlayoffGap.one: The playoff line: {n} point to make up on {pos}.
stakesPlayoffGap.other: The playoff line: {n} points to make up on {pos}.

stakesPlayoffHold.one: You hold a playoff place, {n} point inside the line.
stakesPlayoffHold.other: You hold a playoff place, {n} points inside the line.

matchday.stakesPos: {pos} in the {comp} on {pts} points - {above} above by {gapUp}.
matchday.stakesPosBoth: {pos} in the {comp} on {pts} points - {above} above by {gapUp}, {below} below by {gapDown}.
matchday.stakesRelBar: The relegation playoff. Eighty minutes for a Premier Division place: the winner plays top-flight rugby next season, the loser spends a year in the Championship.
matchday.stakesSlip: Slip up and the top spot is there to be taken.
matchday.stakesTopClear: Top of the {comp} on {pts} points, {gap} clear of {club}.
matchday.streakLossesRest: to this lot - somebody has to break the hoodoo.
matchday.streakWinsRest: over them - the streak is yours to protect.
matchday.tapAName: - tap a name to see what it does
matchday.tapSwapHint: tap a player, tap another to swap · tap twice for the squad list
matchday.tapSwapHintTest: tap a player, tap another to swap · tap twice for the full squad

tenseKick.one: A KICK IN IT · {n} MINUTE LEFT
tenseKick.other: A KICK IN IT · {n} MINUTES LEFT

tenseScore.one: ONE SCORE IN IT · {n} MINUTE LEFT
tenseScore.other: ONE SCORE IN IT · {n} MINUTES LEFT

matchday.respectLine: They respect you now: expect a tighter, more defensive game.
matchday.respectAt_scrum: Their coach will keep it tight and test your scrum.
matchday.respectAt_lineout: Their coach will kick to touch and test your lineout.
matchday.respectAt_breakdown: Their coach will contest your breakdown.
matchday.respectAt_kicking: Their coach will put the high ball up at your back three.
matchday.respectAt_defence: Their coach will go wide to test your defence.
matchday.vdBeaten: Beaten in every collision. The review will be honest, and it will sting.
matchday.vdDraw: A draw that will feel like a loss or a win by Tuesday, depending on the video.
matchday.vdHabit: Winning tight ones is a habit - and we just fed the habit.
matchday.vdMargins: Fine margins. Fix the two below and that is our game.
matchday.vdRuthless: Ruthless. The assistant wants the same standards next week, not a lap of honour.
matchday.vdWasted: All that ball and nothing to show for it - the assistant circles our finishing in red.
matchday.vdWonNoBall: We won without the ball - the defensive shift was enormous. Take that anywhere.
matchday.vmFullD: The commentary and live stats as it happens, with the pitch for tries and the big moments. Every touchline call is yours.
matchday.vmHighlightsD: The ticker stops for scores, cards and injuries only. Half-time and the hour are still yours.
matchday.vmInstantD: He takes the touchline and you read the report. Straight to the result.

matchday.warnNoSpeech: No dressing-room speech chosen - the players will make their own minds up.

matchday.warnScrumFew: Scrum problem: your matchday squad has only {n} different players who can play in the front row, and the referee needs {need}. Short of that he makes every scrum uncontested - no pushing, and a strong pack counts for nothing. Put more front-row cover on the bench.
matchday.warnSixPointer: SIX-POINTER: {gap} and fighting for the same prize. Beat them and bury them.
matchday.warnTurnaround: Only a {n}-day turnaround since the last match - the squad recovered slower this week. Watch the tanks.
matchday.warnUnfit: {player} is only {pct}% fit - his tank will empty early.

matchday.farewellAway_f: This is your last trip to face her on her own patch. Great players deserve a great send-off. Just not the winning kind.
matchday.farewellHome_f: This is the final time {club} bring her to your ground. Beat her, then applaud her off.

matchday.warnUnfit_f: {player} is only {pct}% fit - her tank will empty early.
matchday.assistantTakes_w: {home} v {away} is your assistant's afternoon. She picks the side and files her report - yours is the Test.
matchday.pressureTitle: How much either side is threatening right now - it builds through a spell and fades when nothing comes of it
matchday.wxFxDry: A dry ball and a firm footing: a day for the handling game.
matchday.wxFxDamp: A greasy ball: expect a few more knock-ons, and the boot and the carry come into it.
matchday.wxFxRain: A wet ball: more handling errors, most of all for the sides that throw it about. A day for the boot, the maul and the tackle that holds the carrier up.
matchday.wxFxWind: The wind will take the long kicks and the kicks at goal: keep it in hand when you are playing into it.
matchday.wxFxSnow: Snow on the ground: the ball will be a bar of soap, and tight rugby wins.
matchday.surfFx_grass: A natural surface: softer underfoot, and slower when it rains.
matchday.surfFx_hybrid: Grass stitched with fibre: true and firm, whatever the weather.
matchday.surfFx_artificial: Hard and fast underfoot: it drains well, every collision costs a little more, and the home side knows its bounce.
matchday.htPensBin: {n} penalties already and {ref} is counting: one more at the ruck and somebody sits ten minutes.
matchday.htRefTight: The breakdown is being refereed tight: fewer bodies in the ruck, and hands off the ball.
matchday.htRefLoose: {ref} is letting the breakdown go: get a body over the ball and we can win it back.
matchday.htWetHands: The ball is like soap out there and we keep putting it down: keep it tight and kick for the corners.
matchday.htWetTight: It is wet: one pass too many is a turnover. Carry it, and use the boot.
matchday.htWind: The wind is taking the long kicks: find touch short and keep it in hand into it.
matchday.htUncontested: The scrums are uncontested now: the set piece is out of it, so play off the lineout.
matchday.htScrumBad: Their scrum is on top: get the ball in and out quickly at the set piece.
matchday.htScrumGood: Our scrum is winning: kick for the corners and take them on up front.
matchday.htDefWorks: The defence keeps winning the ball back: hold the line where it is.

tacticsScreen.condCoach: The conditioning coach wants a word

condLine.one: {n} week running at the same extreme on {dial}. The GPS numbers say the squad is running {pct}% hotter than it should, and the last twenty minutes are where you feel that. The league reads a manager who repeats himself, too. Two weeks nearer the middle walks both back.
condLine.other: {n} weeks running at the same extreme on {dial}. The GPS numbers say the squad is running {pct}% hotter than it should, and the last twenty minutes are where you feel that. The league reads a manager who repeats himself, too. Two weeks nearer the middle walks both back.

tacticsScreen.rolesNote: Tap a shirt to set their role.
tacticsScreen.setPieceRuleRest: Calls you use improve each week; calls you do not use get worse. Set-Piece Work in Prep speeds this up, and your scrum coach sets the limit.
tacticsScreen.kickerNote: The first kicker takes every kick. The second takes over if the first is off the pitch.
tacticsScreen.kickerSheetSub: By goal kicking, the whole squad.
tacticsScreen.exitBoxDesc: The safest exit, but you give them the ball.
tacticsScreen.exitLongDesc: Kick for field position. Safe and simple.
tacticsScreen.exitCounterDesc: Keep the ball and run. Risky in your own half.
tacticsScreen.exitFifty22Desc: A 50:22 attempt. Big gain if accurate, loses ground if not.
tacticsScreen.penCornerDesc: Back the maul. Tries win knockouts.
tacticsScreen.penTapDesc: Tap and go, running the play in your Playbook's Penalty slot. Fast, but more errors.
tacticsScreen.noFrontRow: No front-row cover on the bench.
tacticsScreen.law3: If a side cannot field a hooker and two props, scrums become uncontested for both sides. The 16, 17 and 18 shirts cover the front row.
tacticsScreen.splitMismatch: You chose {want}, but the players on the bench make it {got}. The bench that plays is the one you pick.
tacticsScreen.the23Sub: the first three cover the front row
tacticsScreen.bclockSplit: The split takes effect at about 64 minutes. It counts the replacements on the pitch at that moment: three or more gives the full effect, fewer gives part of it.
tacticsScreen.bclockSplitNeutral: Five and Three changes nothing late on. Six and Two or Four and Four take effect at about 64 minutes, counting the replacements on the pitch then: three or more gives the full effect.
tacticsScreen.bclockBriefs: Only the first three replacements sent on with a brief other than Same job play to it. Save the briefs for the changes you will make first.
tacticsScreen.prepSetpieceLong: Scrum and lineout +4%, attack −1% next match.
tacticsScreen.prepFitnessLong: Players tire about 8% slower next match.
tacticsScreen.prepRecoveryLong: Everyone recovers extra condition this week.
tacticsScreen.prepNone: No focus set. Pick one above.
tacticsScreen.quickGamePlansSub: one tap sets all four sliders
tacticsScreen.withTheBallSub: how you attack with the ball
tacticsScreen.withoutTheBallSub: how the line defends when they have it
tacticsScreen.planSaveTitle: Save the current settings: sliders, defence, set-piece calls, kickers and exits.
tacticsScreen.planOverTitle: Replace Plan {n} with the current settings
tacticsScreen.kickTerritoryDesc: Kick to touch for field position. Best if your lineout is stronger.
tacticsScreen.kickContestDesc: High kicks to win the ball back. Good in the wet, gives the ball away in the dry.
tacticsScreen.kickAttackDesc: Grubbers and cross-kicks. Good against a rush defence; loses territory and is poor in the wet.
tacticsScreen.kickBalancedDesc: A mix of kicks. No strength, no weakness.

staff.roleAssistantDesc: Sharper sessions - bigger training gains, faster youth growth, better auto-picked sides.
staff.rolePhysioDesc: Shorter injury layoffs and quicker recovery between matches.
staff.roleScoutDesc: Faster, wider scouting knowledge across the leagues.
staff.roleAttackDesc: Strike moves and shape - a sharper attack every matchday, bigger attacking training gains.
staff.roleDefenceDesc: Line speed and system - a meaner defence every matchday, bigger defensive training gains.
staff.roleScrumCoachDesc: Scrum and lineout platform - the tight five win you matchday penalties.
staff.roleKickingDesc: Territory and the tee - better tactical kicking and goal kicking under pressure.
staff.roleAcademyCoachDesc: Runs the second squad - academy prospects develop faster under a proper mentor.

challenges.sapiacDesc: Tiny Montauban are back in the Elite 14 with the smallest budget in the land. Keep them up. Become immortal in the Tarn-et-Garonne.
challenges.redbullDesc: New owners, big ambitions, bottom-four squad. Turn Newcastle from perennial strugglers into Premier Division champions.
challenges.dynastyDesc: Leinster hoover up every trophy in Ireland. From Thormond Park, end their reign - win the UPC and the Continental Cup.
challenges.piratesDesc: Penzance to the Premier Division: take Cornwall RFC out of the Championship on a shoestring and put the county in the top flight at last.
challenges.ealingDesc: Ealing were given a place in the Premier Division, a budget and a squad bought in a hurry. They have won nothing yet. Win the league twice.
challenges.licenceDesc: Sale finished bottom of the Premier Division. Nobody is relegated here, so the licence is judged on results alone. Finish in the top four and the place is safe.
challenges.grudgeDesc: Lichfield were passed over when the top flight was picked, and there is no promotion out of the second tier. Win the Championship and make them impossible to ignore.
challenges.circusDesc: Gloucester have won the last three, and the whole game travels with them now - the cameras, the sell-outs, the parade. Sarries have the squad and the history to end it. Win the Premier Division, and leave with a winning record over them.

profile.teamTalkWorth: A team talk is worth {pct}% of its full effect while they feel like this. Win and it climbs; lose and it slides.
profile.drillLonger: Training patterns take {pct}% longer to drill while it lasts.
profile.natOffer: {nat} want you as national head coach
profile.natOfferBody: Coach the national side alongside your club. In Test windows you take charge on match day when your club is free - and every championship they win goes in your trophy cabinet.
profile.testWeeksYours: Test weeks are yours when the club calendar allows.
profile.challengeLive: The challenge is live. Judged at each season's end.
profile.decisionsSub: what you chose, and what it did
profile.bareShelves: Bare shelves - for now. Go and fill them.
profile.firstSeason: Your first season is still being written.
profile.specYouthDesc: Trusts the academy and makes kids into men.
profile.specDealerDesc: Lives on the phone. The market bends to him.
profile.specTacticianDesc: Wins the chess match more often than not.
profile.specTacticianHint: Keep a 60% win rate over 20+ matches.
profile.specEuroDesc_f: Won the biggest prize in the club game.
profile.specManmanDesc: Players run through walls for him.
profile.specSurvivorDesc: Boards come and go; he remains.
profile.specMiracleDesc: Won it all with a club nobody backed.
profile.specMiracleHint: Win a league title with an unfancied club.
profile.trustWall: They would run through a wall
profile.trustDisbelief: They do not believe a word
profile.standCarries: Your name carries this room before you say a word.
profile.standFaceValue: The room takes you at face value. Results will do the talking.
profile.standSomeAsk: A few senior heads still ask who you are. Keep winning and they will stop.
profile.standOutranks: The room outranks your record and trains like it knows it.
profile.standNoName: A squad of internationals, a manager without a name: every instruction is quietly re-examined.

report.tut1b: 1. One button moves the game on.
report.tut1: It says {continue} at the top of the screen. Press it and a day goes by. Press it again and again and you walk through the week - who is injured, what the press want, who is for sale - until Saturday, when the button says {matchday}.
report.tut2: Tap the clipboard at the bottom, then {team} - you land on the team sheet. Tap two players to swap them, or press {bestXV} and let your assistant draft one - then change anything you disagree with. You have fifteen starters and eight replacements.
report.tut3: Press {kickOff}. You say a few words to the players first - pick whichever one feels right, there is no wrong answer. During the game you can bring on replacements or change how you play. When you win a penalty near their line, you choose: kick at the posts for three points, or go to the corner and try for a try.
report.tut4: Every number in this game has a page explaining it, in plain English, in {handbook} (bottom right, Manager). It has a search box. If something confuses you, it is in there.
report.tut5: Find out. A lost Saturday is not you doing it wrong - it is the other side turning up. The board tells you what it expects on the Finances screen, and you have a season to deliver it.
report.crashBody: Your save is safe. The game writes to this device every week, so the worst you can lose is what has happened since the last Continue. Going back to the title screen usually clears it, because it is almost always one screen misreading something rather than the save itself.
report.crashNote: Report this attaches that message, the build and the screens you came through - you do not have to copy anything down.
