comm.tmoNoTry2: NO TRY! A knock-on in the build-up, and the try is chalked off. {team} are furious.
comm.tmoNoTry3: NO TRY! The final pass was forward. {team} have to go again.
comm.tmoNoTry4: NO TRY! A foot in touch before the grounding. {team} are denied.
comm.tmoReviewFwd1: {team} are over, but the referee wants a look upstairs: was the pass in the build-up forward?
comm.tmoReviewFwd2: {team} celebrate, but the TMO is checking a pass back in the build-up.
comm.tmoNoTryFwd1: NO TRY! The TMO finds a forward pass in the build-up. {team} are denied.
comm.tmoNoTryFwd2: NO TRY! The replays show the pass drifting forward in the build-up, and the try is chalked off. {team} can hardly argue.
comm.tmoFwdScrum1: Scrum to {team} for the forward pass, back where it was thrown.
comm.tmoFwdScrum2: The try is gone, and {team} have the put-in at the scrum for the forward pass.
comm.tmoFwdStands1: The TMO lets it stand: not clearly forward. The replays will be argued over all week.
comm.tmoFwdStands2: It stands! A tight call on the pass in the build-up, and {team} will not care how it looked.
comm.moveCallLo1: {team} win their lineout and call the {move_k}.
comm.moveCallLo2: Clean ball off the top, and {team} have a move on: the {move_k}.
comm.moveCallLo3: {team} set up the {move_k} off their own throw.
comm.moveCallSc1: Scrum to {team}, and the backs line up for the {move_k}.
comm.moveCallSc2: {team} hold it at the base of the scrum and go to the {move_k}.
comm.moveCallTap1: Penalty to {team} in the 22, and they tap it quickly: the {move_k}.
comm.moveCallTap2: {team} take the quick tap and go to the {move_k}.
comm.moveShape1: {team} settle into the {move_k}, forwards spread across the field.
comm.moveShape2: Phase after phase from {team} out of the {move_k}.
comm.moveShape3: {team} work the {move_k} and keep going forward.
comm.moveMisfire1: The {move_k} goes wrong: {player} is caught behind the gain line.
comm.moveMisfire2: {opp} read the {move_k}, and {player} is driven backwards.
comm.moveMisfire3: {player} runs the {move_k}, but the timing is off and it goes to ground.
comm.moveMisfire4: The {move_k} is snuffed out before it starts. {team} go backwards.
comm.moveGain1: The {move_k} works: {player} gets {team} over the gain line.
comm.moveGain2: {player} runs the {move_k} well, and {team} make good ground.
comm.shapeMisfire1: {opp} are up quickly on the {move_k}, and {team} go backwards.
comm.shapeMisfire2: The {move_k} is not working for {team}: they are stopped behind the line.
comm.moveTryLo1: TRY! Straight off the lineout, the {move_k} from {maker} puts {player} through!
comm.moveTryLo2: TRY! A training-ground score: the {move_k} off the lineout, {maker} with the key pass and {player} over the line.
comm.moveTryLo3: TRY! Lineout, the {move_k}, and {player} is through the gap from the pass by {maker}!
comm.moveTryLoSelf: TRY! The {move_k} off the lineout, and {player} runs it and finishes it!
comm.moveTrySc1: TRY! From the scrum, the {move_k} from {maker} puts {player} through!
comm.moveTrySc2: TRY! Scrum, the {move_k}, and over. {maker} runs it, {player} finishes it.
comm.moveTrySc3: TRY! The {move_k} off the scrum splits them open, and {player} takes the pass from {maker} to score!
comm.moveTryScSelf: TRY! {player} runs the {move_k} off the scrum and goes all the way!
comm.moveTryTap1: TRY! Quick tap, the {move_k}, and {maker} sends {player} over!
comm.moveTryTap2: TRY! They tap and go: the {move_k}, {maker} with the pass and {player} over the line!
comm.moveTryTap3: TRY! The {move_k} from the tap penalty, and {player} goes over from the pass by {maker}!
comm.moveTryTapSelf: TRY! {player} takes the tap, runs the {move_k} and finishes it!
comm.shapeTry1: TRY! The {move_k} has been grinding them down, and {player} finally goes over from the pass by {maker}!
comm.shapeTry2: TRY! Out of the {move_k}, {maker} finds {player} on the edge!
comm.shapeTry3: TRY! Phase after phase in the {move_k}, and {player} goes over from the pass by {maker}!
comm.shapeTrySelf: TRY! {player} carries off the {move_k} and forces it over!
comm.penWide: The kicker pushes the penalty attempt wide.
comm.tryPackDrive: TRY! The pack drives over the line!
comm.tryMaulRumbles: TRY! The maul rumbles over and {player} grounds it!
comm.tryCareerMilestone: Career try number {n} for {player}! Both sets of supporters know a milestone when they see one: the applause takes a while to die down.
comm.trySeasonCount: That's try number {n} of the season for {player} - some campaign he's having.
comm.tryAtTestimonial: Of all the people. {player} scores at his own testimonial and the ground refuses to sit down. Write the script yourself. You could not do better.
comm.tryNoCelebration: No celebration from {player} against his old club - hands raised in apology, but the damage is done.
comm.tryRetiringOvation: The whole ground rises for {player} - friend and foe alike. He retires in the summer, and nobody here wants to forget watching him do that.
comm.tryComeback: {player} scores on the comeback trail - weeks of rehab, tackle bags and dark mornings, and that try is the answer to all of it. Look at his face.
comm.maulToCorner: To the corner! The maul assembles five metres out...
comm.maulHeldUp: Held up! {team} survive and win the scrum.
comm.maulRepelledPenalty: They repel the maul but concede another penalty - pressure stays on.
comm.quickTapPhases: Quick tap! {team} go through the phases, camped on the line...
comm.benchSixTwo: {team} have emptied a six-two bench. Everything from here goes through the middle.
comm.benchFiveThree: {team} have four fresh backs on. They will try to win this in the wide channels.
comm.outOfCover: {team} are out of cover. {player}, a {pos}, finishes the game at {shirt} and both sides know it.
comm.heavyKnock: {player} takes a heavy knock - he waves the physio away, but he's moving gingerly.
comm.injuryRushedBack: He was rushed back too soon.
comm.subChangeOfPlan: Change of plan on the touchline: {on} goes on instead of {off}.{brief_k}
comm.briefImpact: He is on to go through them.
comm.briefShore: He is on to shut the door.
comm.briefManage: He is on to play the corners and kill the clock.
comm.ycRepeated: Repeated infringements! That's {n} penalties against {team} and the referee has seen enough. {player} takes ten in the bin for the team.
comm.penKickableAsk: PENALTY to {team} - kickable range. The captain looks to the touchline for the call...
comm.dropMiss1: {player} drops for goal, but it slides wide of the posts.
comm.dropMiss2: Drop goal attempt from {player}... and it is wide. Twenty-two drop-out.
comm.dropMiss3: {player} goes for the drop goal and snatches at it. No good.
comm.dropMiss4: {player} tries a snap drop from the pocket. It falls short and is touched down.
comm.dropMiss5: Up goes the drop goal from {player}... it hits the upright and bounces away!
comm.yellowCard: Yellow card - {player} to the bin for ten.
comm.hiaFailed: {player} FAILS his Head Injury Assessment - concussion protocols, no further part. {sub} stays on.
comm.hiaPassed: {player} passes his HIA and jogs back into the fray.
comm.hiaLedAway: {player} is led away for a Head Injury Assessment - {sub} on while the doctors do their work.
comm.fun1: A dog has made it onto the pitch and is being chased by two stewards and a very keen {team} replacement. The dog is winning.
comm.fun2: The ball smacks the referee square in the back. Play on, says the referee, as if nothing whatsoever happened.
comm.fun3: {player} calls for the ball, gets it, and looks genuinely surprised about it.
comm.fun4: A seagull lands on the halfway line and stays for two phases. Nobody asks it to move.
comm.fun5: The stadium announcer reads out a lost car key. Half the {team} bench checks their pockets.
comm.fun6: {player} loses a boot in the tackle and plays three phases in one. The boot gets a round of applause when it comes back.
comm.howler1: {player} drops the ball over the line with the try begging! White-line fever at its cruellest.
comm.howler2: {player} kicks it dead from halfway - absolutely nothing on. The coach turns away.
comm.howler3: Oh no - {player} throws a wild offload straight to the opposition. Cheap turnover.
comm.howler4: {player} completely misses the restart. It bounces once and rolls into touch. Chaos.
comm.howler5: {player} runs a lap of honour before grounding it... and the cover knocks it loose! Unforgivable.
comm.halfTimeNumbers: First-half numbers: possession {hposs}%–{aposs}%, tries {htries}–{atries}, penalty goals {hpens}–{apens}.
comm.hourMark: Hour mark - a lull in play. Time to change the picture from the sideline.
comm.doesWidth: push their wings out to meet it, and thin out the rucks to do so.
comm.seesMiddle: everything is coming through the middle
comm.doesMiddle: stack the breakdown and dare the ball to go wide.
comm.doesAerial: drop a man deep and keep the back three home.
comm.doesPace: slow everything - every scrum reset, every mark, every tying of a bootlace.
comm.doesPhysical: refuse the scrap, keep fifteen on the field and let the referee do the tidying.
comm.doesPassive: raise the tempo and force the game to be played.
comm.coachChases: {who} has seen enough - shackles off, bench emptied. {team} will run everything as they chase the game.
comm.coachManages: {who} signals to the corners: game management time. {team} will strangle the clock from here.
comm.subUndoneNamed: Change of heart on the touchline: {off} stays on and {on} sits back down.
comm.subUndone: Change of heart on the touchline: {off} stays on and the replacement sits back down.
comm.shirtSwap: Positional switch for {team}: {a} and {b} swap shirts.
comm.forfeit: Walkover: {loser} could not raise a side. {winner} take the match 28-0.
comm.uncontestedNow: {team} have lost {player} from the front row with nobody trained to cover him: the referee orders UNCONTESTED SCRUMS from here. No shove, no scrum penalties.
comm.uncontestedShort: And it costs {team} a second player: under Law 3.20 a side that goes uncontested through a card must take another man off. {player} makes way.
comm.contestedAgain: The front-rower is back from the bin and so is the cover: the referee restores CONTESTED SCRUMS.
comm.frontRowReturns: The bench is spent, so {player} comes back on: a replaced front-rower may return for an injured one, and the scrum stays a contest.
comm.frontRowBinCover: {lost} is in the bin and {team} need a trained front row, so under Law 3 {on} comes on and {player} leaves the field to make way until the ten minutes are up. The scrum stays a contest.
comm.frontRowRedCover: {lost} is gone for the match and {team} need a trained front row, so under Law 3 {on} comes on and {player} leaves the field to make way for the rest of it. The scrum stays a contest, and {team} are still a player down.
comm.frontRowBinBack: {lost} is back from the bin and takes the front-row shirt back from {on}, who returns to the bench; {player} comes back on too.
comm.testimonial_f: {player}'s testimonial. She leads the teams out with her kids at her side, the ground on its feet, scarves above every head. Then the whistle blows and it is a rugby match again.
comm.oldBoy_f: A familiar face out there: {player} lines up against {oldClub}, where she made {n} appearances. {tail_k}
comm.oldBoyKnowsThem_f: She knows this opposition inside out.
comm.milestoneApps_f: A milestone afternoon: {player} makes career appearance number {n}. The tunnel applauds her out; the scoreboard will not care.
comm.try9_f: TRY! {player} arcs outside her marker and won't be caught!
comm.try11_f: TRY! A monstrous fend from {player} and she strolls in!
comm.try18_f: TRY! {player} bumps off three tacklers on her way to the line!
comm.try19_f: TRY! {player} shows and goes - nobody within five metres of her!
comm.try21_f: TRY! {player} straightens, sits the last defender down and strolls under the sticks!
comm.try22_f: TRY! The blindside wing comes off her line and it is {player} who finishes it!
comm.pen5_f: {player} takes her time... and drills it.
comm.pen11_f: {player} wipes the mud off the ball, wipes the rain off her face, and nails it.
comm.flavGrass4_f: Huge cheer from the clubhouse balcony as {player} flattens her opposite number. Someone rings the bell.
comm.flavPac6_f: One-handed take above her head from {player}, under pressure, in traffic. No notes.
comm.flav12_f: Choke tackle! {player} holds her up and it's a {team} scrum.
comm.flav22_f: {player} throws a cut-out pass that misses three women - vision, that.
comm.flavDerby5_f: {player} and her opposite number exchange words at the lineout. Neither is discussing the weather.
comm.tired1_f: {player} has her hands on her knees - the tank is emptying.
comm.tired4_f: Cramp for {player} - she waves away the physio, but the legs have gone.
comm.trySeasonCount_f: That's try number {n} of the season for {player} - some campaign she's having.
comm.tryAtTestimonial_f: Of all the people. {player} scores at her own testimonial and the ground refuses to sit down. Write the script yourself. You could not do better.
comm.tryNoCelebration_f: No celebration from {player} against her old club - hands raised in apology, but the damage is done.
comm.tryRetiringOvation_f: The whole ground rises for {player} - friend and foe alike. She retires in the summer, and nobody here wants to forget watching her do that.
comm.tryComeback_f: {player} scores on the comeback trail - weeks of rehab, tackle bags and dark mornings, and that try is the answer to all of it. Look at her face.
comm.heavyKnock_f: {player} takes a heavy knock - she waves the physio away, but she's moving gingerly.
comm.injuryRushedBack_f: She was rushed back too soon.
comm.briefImpact_f: She is on to go through them.
comm.briefShore_f: She is on to shut the door.
comm.briefManage_f: She is on to play the corners and kill the clock.
comm.hiaFailed_f: {player} FAILS her Head Injury Assessment - concussion protocols, no further part. {sub} stays on.
comm.hiaPassed_f: {player} passes her HIA and jogs back into the fray.
comm.doesAerial_f: drop a woman deep and keep the back three home.
comm.uncontestedShort_f: And it costs {team} a second player: under Law 3.20 a side that goes uncontested through a card must take another woman off. {player} makes way.
comm.oppCoachNamed_w: {coach} has done her homework: {team} are set up specifically for {pattern_k}. Change the picture, or play through the plan.
comm.oppCoach_w: The opposition coach has done her homework: {team} are set up specifically for {pattern_k}. Change the picture, or play through the plan.
comm.advPlaying: The arm stays out - advantage {team}, and the whistle never comes...
comm.advOver: Advantage {team}, played to the end of it, and the referee waves it away. Three points gone.
comm.koDamp: A greasy surface after the morning's rain.
comm.uncontestedNoRep: And under Law 3 the player whose departure caused it cannot be replaced: {team} take {player} off and play on with fourteen.
comm.uncontestedBin: And under Law 3 {team} lose a second player while {lost} sits out the ten minutes: {player} goes off too, and the two come back together.
comm.specProp: {player} packs down at prop for {team} without the training for it: the scrum will creak.
comm.specHook: {player} is at hooker for {team} and has never thrown in: the lineout will suffer.
comm.specNine: {player} is at scrum-half for {team}, and it shows: the service from the base is slow.

reply.chatPraiseSarcasm: He squints at you. "Am I being set up here?" The compliment lands like a slap.
reply.chatPraiseLoyal: "Means a lot, boss." He walks out an inch taller.
reply.chatPraiseProfessional: A short nod. "Just doing the job." But he is smiling on the way out.
reply.chatPraiseAmbitious: "About time somebody noticed." He will want more of this.
reply.chatPraiseMercenary: "Cheers, boss. Does the recognition come with a rise?" Only half joking.
reply.chatPraiseLeader: "Save it for the young lads - but thanks." He passes it on within the hour.
reply.chatPraiseDefault: He beams. For once the fire in him is warming the room.
reply.chatWarnInsulted: He stares. "Have you watched the games?" Word of this gets around the dressing room.
reply.chatWarnTakesIt: He takes it on the chin. "You'll see a response on Saturday." You believe him.
reply.chatWarnStung: Stung - but he needed to hear it, and the extras he does that evening say so.
reply.chatWarnShrug: A shrug. "Noted." You suspect it went in one ear and out the other.
reply.chatWarnSlams: He slams the door on the way out. That could go either way on Saturday.

reply.requestGrantedSenior: Granted, and the room went quiet when it heard. {player} was one of theirs.
reply.requestRefused: Refused. {player} stays, and stays unhappy about it.
reply.requestRefusedBadly: Refused, and taken badly. {player} left the office without shaking hands.
reply.requestRefusedBadly_f: Refused, and taken badly. {player} left the office without shaking hands.
reply.boardNo_time: "We back managers who are winning." No. And they will not hear it again for a while.
reply.boardNo_funds: No. The finance director talked about the current account for ten minutes.
reply.boardNo_facilities: No. Build the case on the pitch first.
reply.boardNo_staff: No. Get more out of the ones you have.

boardYes_time.one: The chairman backs you publicly. That is {n} week, whatever the table says.
boardYes_time.other: The chairman backs you publicly. That is {n} weeks, whatever the table says.

reply.boardYes_funds: Approved: {amount} added to the transfer budget.
reply.boardYes_facilities: Approved. The board pays for the next {facility} build - ask for it on Club Infrastructure.
reply.boardYes_staff: Approved: {amount} ring-fenced for the backroom. It pays before the club's own money does.

dream.europeShieldOnly: a Continental Shield on the shelf: the big one is still out there
dream.doubleBoth: both, and nobody can take either back
dream.dynasty: Win the league three seasons running
dream.dynastyLower: win the league three seasons running
dream.dynastyTwo: two in a row: one more
dream.academy: Build a first team out of your own academy
dream.academyLower: build a first team out of your own academy
dream.academyDone: a team of your own making
dream.academyNone: no graduates in the senior squad yet

academySome.one: {n} graduate with senior rugby behind them
academySome.other: {n} graduates with senior rugby behind them

dream.world: Coach a nation to the World Championship
dream.worldLower: coach a nation to the World Championship
dream.worldInTheJob: in the job: now win it
dream.worldOnceHad: you have coached a Test side - get another job and finish it
dream.verdictDone: THE DREAM IS DONE: {title_k}. Whatever comes next is a bonus.

press.campQ1: Pre-season, and the performance staff want a decision. The budget stretches to one special week: a warm-weather camp abroad, a community week at home, or the sponsor's exhibition tour. Which is it?
press.campQ2: Three options are circled on the staff-room whiteboard for the spare pre-season week: the heat camp, the town, or the sponsor's roadshow. The department heads are waiting on you.
press.campHeatR: Flights booked. A week of double sessions in the sun - the squad comes home lean, sharp, and united in their hatred of the hill runs.
press.campHomeR: Schools, junior clubs, open training. Costs nothing, and the town will remember it all season.
press.campTourR: Three airports, two black-tie functions, one glossy cheque. The accountants beam. The players' legs file a formal complaint.
press.punditsSplit: The pundits are split on you.
press.stanceQ1: Season launch day, and the room wants a number. {pred_k} Where are you telling this club it is going?
press.stanceQ2: The chairman, the sponsors and the season-ticket renewal letter all want the same sentence from you. {pred_k} How do you pitch the year?
press.stanceHigh: Judge us in May - aim high (+{fund} war chest)
press.stanceHighR: The headline writes itself and the board puts {fund} behind it - beat the pundits' number or that money comes back out of next summer's budget, with interest. {room_k} From here every win is proof and every defeat is a broken promise: the boardroom needle will swing hard, both ways, all season.
press.stanceHighUnrated: Nobody rated this squad, and the dressing room walks a foot taller for hearing a manager who does.
press.stanceHighExpected: The dressing room nods along - a club this size expects the talk.
press.stanceBoardR: Steady. You and the board are reading from the same page, and results will be judged the way they always were.
press.stanceSafeR: You talk the year down to take the heat off the group. The boardroom needle is muted both ways: defeats cost less, but so does winning - credit is thin for a man who promised nothing.{tail_k}
press.stanceSafeFancied: And at a club the pundits fancy, the squad hears something else in it: a manager who does not believe in them.
press.loanBlocked: Agreed in principle, but it stops there for now. {why}
press.silverDoubleQ1: The table in front of you has {n} trophies on it. {what_cl}, in one weekend. The room is on its feet before the first question: how does a season like this happen?
press.silverDoubleQ2: Nobody in this room has covered a weekend like it: {what_cl}, back to back. When does it sink in?
press.silverOneQ1: The {what_cl} is on the table in front of you, still wearing its ribbons. The room wants the story: what wins a final?
press.silverOneQ2: The champagne is barely dry on the {what_cl}. Where does this one rank in your career?
press.silverGroupR: The quote runs under every photo of the celebrations. The squad walks into pre-season believing, and the chairman has the front page framed.
press.silverFansR: The town takes it personally, in the best way. Season-ticket renewals do not need a letter this year.
press.silverAgain: We go again - this is a beginning
press.silverAgainR: Half the room writes “dynasty”. The board hears ambition and likes the sound of it; the squad hears the bar going up.
press.courtQ1: Every outlet leads with the same story: {club} have you on their shortlist. The room goes quiet. Are you staying?
press.courtQ2: The first hand up does not bother with the rugby. “{club} want you, and everyone in this room knows it. Are you staying?”
press.courtQ3: {poss} interest in you is on every back page this morning. The room leans forward as one. What is your answer?
press.courtStayR: The clip runs on every channel by teatime. The chairman texts a thumbs up; the squad trains like a weight came off. {short} move down their list.
press.courtWork: We have work to do here
press.courtWorkR: Measured, professional, just short of a promise. The story cools without quite dying.
press.courtNeverR: A stonewall the whole room hears as a maybe. The chairman's silence is loud, and the dressing room wonders if the gaffer is half out the door.
press.banQ1: The citing commissioner has upheld {player}'s red card: a {n}-match ban. The club has 48 hours to appeal. Do you?

banQ2.one: {player}'s suspension is confirmed this morning - {n} match. Half your inbox is lawyers who fancy the footage. Appeal it?
banQ2.other: {player}'s suspension is confirmed this morning - {n} matches. Half your inbox is lawyers who fancy the footage. Appeal it?

banQ3.one: The panel was not moved: {n} match for {player}. The supporters call it a stitch-up. Fight it, or take it?
banQ3.other: The panel was not moved: {n} matches for {player}. The supporters call it a stitch-up. Fight it, or take it?

press.banAppealR: The paperwork goes in overnight and the hearing is fast-tracked. The verdict lands in your inbox the same day.
press.banAcceptR: No circus, no lawyers. The panel notes the club's professionalism, and the player serves his time quietly.
press.banBlastR: The dressing room loves it. The league office adds a note to your file, and the next fifty-fifty call may remember this.
press.finalQ1: Finals week. The room is three deep, half of them faces you have never seen. {comp}, {where}, {opp} on the other side. The first question is the only one they all came for: can you win it?
press.finalQ2: The camera count has tripled and there is a national broadcaster's anchor in the front row. One game, at {where}, against {opp}, for the {comp}. How do you handle a week like this?
press.finalQ3: Every seat taken, standing at the back - finals week does this. {opp} at {where} for the {comp}. They want a headline. What do you give them?
press.finalWin: We are ready. We will win it
press.finalWinR: The back pages have their headline and the dressing room walks taller all week. If Saturday goes wrong, that sentence will be read back to you for years.
press.finalRespectR: Measured and confident. The board approves, the players nod along, and nobody has been handed a team-talk quote.
press.finalTrap: The occasion is the trap - it is just rugby
press.finalTrapR: You talk the week down to protect the group. Sensible - though one or two of the younger lads wanted to hear the fire.
press.hotQ1: {player} has been in scintillating form - some are calling him the best {pos_k} in the competition. Do you agree?
press.hotQ2: The whole league is purring about {player}. Best {pos_k} in the competition right now: yes or no?
press.hotQ3: {player} again at the weekend. The pundits have run out of superlatives - have you?
press.hotPraiseR: {player} is reportedly delighted with your public backing.
press.hotFeet: Keep his feet on the ground
press.hotFeetR: A measured response. {player} knows there is more to do.
press.hotOthersR: You spread the praise across the whole side. {player} nods along, and the pack notes the mention of the men who win him his ball.
press.noCommentR: The press pack grumbles and moves on.
press.missedR: The moment passed. The outlet ran the piece without you, and next week brings new questions.
press.coldQ1: {player} has looked well short of his best in recent weeks. Is his place under threat?
press.coldQ2: Be honest about {player} - the supporters on the message boards already are. What is going wrong for him?
press.coldQ3: {player} would struggle to make most sides in this league on current form. Does he keep the shirt?
press.coldBackR: {player} appreciates the show of faith and vows to repay it.
press.coldAdmitR: Honest, but {player} is stung by the criticism.
press.coldBlameR: “If he is short of form, look at how I am using him.” The room did not expect that. {player} did not either, and he trains like a man with a debt to repay.
press.coldNoOneR: You deflect the question with a straight bat.
press.rumourQ1: We're hearing strong links between {player} and {club}. What's your message to worried supporters?
press.rumourQ2: {club} scouts were in the stand again, and everyone knows who they came to watch. Is {player} for sale?
press.rumourQ3: {player} to {club} is the story that will not die. Kill it now, if you can.
press.rumourNeverR: A firm line. {player} feels wanted; {short} are said to be undeterred.
press.rumourPriceR: {player}'s agent has taken note. Expect the phone to ring.
press.rumourAsk: Ask him - he is happy here
press.rumourAskR: You hand the question to the player, publicly and warmly. {player} obliges with a straight answer about loving the club, which buries the story better than any denial of yours could.
press.derbyQ1: {derby} this weekend. {opp_k} say the pressure is all on you. Your response?
press.derbyQ2: It is {derby} week and the town talks of nothing else. {opp_k} reckon the pressure sits with you. Does it?
press.derbyQ3: {poss_k} players have been talking in the papers all week ahead of {derby}. Rise to it, or rise above it?
press.derbyFanR: The back pages love it. The town is at boiling point - your players will feel ten feet tall, or feel the heat.
press.derbyJustR: Nobody believes you, least of all your own supporters.
press.derbyPraiseR: A statesmanlike answer. Both sets of fans nod approvingly, then go back to hating each other.
press.kidQ1: Everyone is talking about {player} - {age} years old and lighting up the league. Is he the future of the club?
press.kidQ2: {player}, {age}, and already the first name the supporters sing. How good can he actually be?
press.kidQ3: Scouts, agents, pundits: all of them asking about {player}. Is the club ready for what comes next?
press.kidCrownR: {player} floats out of the press room - and every scout in the hemisphere just circled his name.
press.kidProtectR: Measured. He keeps developing away from the circus.
press.kidEarn: He plays when he earns it
press.kidEarnR: Old school. {player} bristles, but the senior players approve.
press.raceQ1: The title race is down to you and {club}. {coach_k} says his side “handles the big moments better”. Care to respond?
press.raceQ2: {coach_k} lit the fuse this morning: his {short} side “handles the big moments better”, apparently. Your reply?
press.raceQ3: Two horses left in this race, and the other one is {club}. They are talking a big game across town. Anything to send back?
press.racePressureR: “{short} have everything to lose - we're loving this.” The squad walks taller; the run-in just got personal.
press.raceOurselvesR: Calm, professional, forgettable. The dressing room stays level.
press.raceFlatterR: You call {short} “the best side in the league”. Pundits call it mind games. Maybe it is.
press.unveilQ1: {player} is in the room for his unveiling, shirt in hand. What are you expecting from your new {pos_k}?
press.unveilQ2: New shirt, new number, cameras everywhere: {player} is officially yours. What did you sign him to do?
press.unveilQ3: {player} has just finished posing for the photographers. Tell the supporters what their new {pos_k} brings.
press.unveilMarqueeR: “He changes everything for us.” {player} beams - and every match report this season will measure him against that sentence.
press.unveilSettleR: Sensible. The pressure valve stays closed while he learns the calls.
press.unveilFightR: A cold shower at his own unveiling. The squad notes that nobody gets given a shirt here.
press.crisisQ1: {n} defeats in the last {of}. Supporters are restless. How do you respond to talk of a crisis?
press.crisisQ2: {n} losses from {of}. The word “crisis” was said on the radio this morning. Is it one?
press.crisisQ3: The table does not lie: beaten {n} times in your last {of}. What do you say to supporters who have stopped believing?
press.crisisOwnR: The dressing room respects your honesty.
press.crisisMarginsR: The board is unimpressed with excuses.
press.crisisAttackR: The clip goes viral for the wrong reasons.
press.cardsQ1: {n} cards at the weekend, {man_k} among them. Is there a discipline problem in your squad?
press.cardsQ2: {Man_k} in the book again - {n} cards in one afternoon. When does passion become a problem?
press.cardsQ3: The disciplinary summary makes grim reading: {n} cards. Whose fault is that - the players' or the coaching?
press.cardsDefendR: The squad appreciates the shield. The disciplinary panel does not.
press.cardsAddressR: Sternly said. Extra tackling-technique sessions are already booked.
press.cardsBlameR: The players love it; the league office sends a warning letter.
press.ownerQ1: The takeover is done and the new owner is in the building. Every manager in your position is one bad month from a “restructure”. What is your message to him?
press.ownerQ2: New owner, first week. History says managers rarely survive a regime change. Why will you be different?
press.ownerQ3: The new owner watched training from the balcony this morning, arms folded. What does he need to hear from you?
press.ownerRugbyR: Confident, direct - owners like a man who volunteers for the scoreboard.
press.ownerVision: We are aligned on the vision
press.ownerVisionR: Fluent boardroom-speak. The suits nod; the terraces roll their eyes.
press.ownerComeGoR: The dressing room loves the defiance. Upstairs, a note is made.
press.vultureQ1: There are reports this morning that the board has sounded out potential replacements. Are you fighting for your job?
press.vultureQ2: Names are circulating for your job - real names, with real agents. Do you still have the board's backing?
press.vultureQ3: A bookmaker suspended betting on the next manager here this morning. How safe are you, honestly?
press.vultureTrophiesR: Defiant. The players walk a little taller - now you have to deliver.
press.vultureBoard: That is a question for the board
press.vultureBoardR: The vacuum fills with more speculation.
press.vultureLaughR: The room chuckles. The chairman, watching the stream, does not.
press.runInSecond: Second, and breathing down their necks
press.runInQ1: Top {where_k} with the season on the line. Can this group handle the pressure of a run-in?
press.runInQ2: {pile_k} with the business end here. Do your players sleep at night?
press.runInQ3: Every week from now is a final. {who_k} always claim to enjoy it - do you, actually?
press.runInTarget: We want the target on our backs
press.runInTargetR: Bold. The bookies shorten your odds; the players feed off it.
press.runInOneGameR: The oldest line in the book, delivered with a straight face.
press.runInPrivilegeR: Instant back-page headline. The town believes.
press.intlQ1: {n} of your players are away on international duty. Should clubs be compensated when the Test windows strip their squads?
press.intlQ2: {n} first-teamers gone to the Test window and half your dressing room is empty. Proud, or fed up?
press.intlQ3: The internationals have taken {n} of yours this window. Is the club-versus-country tug of war broken?
press.intlProudR: Gracious - and the academy parents noticed.
press.intlCalendarR: Half the league's coaches text you in agreement.
press.intlCopeR: Brisk. The fringe players hear the message: their chance is coming.
press.intlFringe: The fringe get their shot now
press.intlFringeR: Ten men who train all week and watch all weekend just sat up straighter.
press.intlMoneyR: The chairman applauds from upstairs. The unions send a lawyer's letter.
press.intlFamiliesR: A warm line that costs nothing and travels. Two mums frame the clipping.
press.intlDepth: Judge my squad depth in May
press.intlDepthR: Confident. The pundits write it down for later, which is how promises work.
press.intlClub: I pick clubs over country, always
press.intlClubR: The terraces love it. Three national coaches stop returning your calls.
press.intlHurtsR: Candid, and the room respects it - but the headline writes itself: COACH ADMITS CRISIS.
press.natQ1: Your {nation_k} squad is in camp and the country is watching. What does this window need to deliver?
press.natQ2: Two jobs, one weekend: the nation's press want to know where {nationThe_k} sits on your list. Well?
press.natQ3: The {nation_k} squad you named has the phone-ins arguing already. Talk us through your thinking.
press.natWinLotR: The union loves it - and has written it down. Deliver, or this window becomes the stick they beat you with.
press.natTestByTestR: Measured. The federation nods; the phone-ins move on to the referees.
press.natClubPaysR: Your dressing room walks taller. In the federation offices, someone underlines a clause.
press.unbeatenQ1: {n} league games, {n} wins. Nobody has laid a glove on you. Go on - say the word.
press.unbeatenQ2: Still unbeaten in the league. What is the secret, and when does the weight of the run start to tell?
press.unbeatenQ3: An unbeaten season is quietly becoming a real conversation. Is it on?
press.unbeatenNothingR: Straight bat. The senior players nod along.
press.unbeatenSayItR: The town roars. The board swallows hard - that quote will follow you into every ground.
press.unbeatenStandard: The run will end. The standard will not
press.unbeatenStandardR: Composed and quotable. Both rooms are happy.
press.plansQ1: {player} knocks and closes the door behind him. “Boss, I have barely played all season. Tell me straight - am I in your plans or not?”
press.plansQ2: {player} has been waiting outside since the end of training. “I watch every session from the sidelines, boss. I need to know if there is a future for me here.”
press.plansQ3: {player} does not sit down. “I am not here to argue. One question: do you see me in this team? Because right now I cannot.”
press.plansIn: You are in my plans - stay ready
press.plansInR1: {player} leaves with his head up. He will hold you to it - pick him soon or this conversation happens again, louder.
press.plansInR2: The tension goes out of his shoulders. A promise in this office is a promise on the team sheet, he will be counting the weeks.
press.plansOut: Honestly? He can find a new club
press.plansOutR1: A hard truth, kindly delivered. {player} thanks you for being straight, and his agent is making calls within the hour.
press.plansOutR2: He goes quiet, then nods. “Appreciate the honesty, boss.” The listing will not shock anyone in the dressing room.
press.plansEarn: Nobody is owed a shirt here
press.plansEarnR1: He nods, jaw tight, and heads back to training. The squad hears about it, the honest ones respect it.
press.plansEarnR2: “Fine. Then I will take one.” He trains like a man possessed all week. That answer either made him or lost him.
press.loanQ1: {player}, {age}, is waiting by your office after training. “I am not learning anything carrying tackle bags, boss. Send me on loan - I need real minutes.”
press.loanQ2: {player} catches you in the corridor, all nerves and rehearsed lines. “Boss, my mates from the age-groups are playing senior rugby every week. I am standing still here. Let me go and prove it somewhere.”
press.loanQ3: The academy coach sends {player} up to see you. The lad gets it out in one breath: “Loan me out, boss. I will come back better - or I will come back and you can tell me I was wrong.”
press.loanMinutesR1: {player} lights up. Play him in the next few weeks or the shine wears off fast.
press.loanMinutesR2: He floats out of the office. A first-team promise at his age is rocket fuel - but it burns fast if the team sheet never shows it.
press.loanAgreeR1: A smart development call. The loan is agreed the same afternoon, and the reports will come back to you every few weeks.
press.loanAgreeR2: He grins and shakes your hand twice, and the academy coach makes the calls before you have changed your mind: minutes make players, benches make excuses.
press.loanStay: He is not ready to leave
press.loanStayR1: He trudges out without a word. The academy coach thinks you have just cooled your hottest prospect.
press.loanStayR2: “Right.” One word, and the door does not slam, which is somehow worse. Keep an eye on his training reports.
press.dealQ1: {player}, {age} now, sits down across from you. “My deal is up this summer. I am not asking for promises, boss - I just need to know if I should be planning a life after this place.”
press.dealQ2: {player} waits until the room is empty. “Twelve years a professional, boss, and this is the conversation you never get used to. My contract is up. Where do I stand?”
press.dealQ3: {player} brings two coffees in and sets one down in front of you. “No agents, no lawyers, just us. My deal ends this summer. Tell me what you are thinking.”
press.dealYear: There is another year in you
press.dealYearR1: {player} shakes your hand hard. Offer the terms from his player page before someone else does.
press.dealYearR2: Relief, then a grin you have not seen since pre-season. Get the paperwork moving before his agent hears anything else.
press.dealLast: This season is his last here
press.dealLastR1: He takes it with dignity. He will finish the job properly - and the young players just saw how endings are handled here.
press.dealLastR2: A long exhale, a nod, a handshake. “Then let us win something on the way out.” Class to the end.
press.dealWaitR1: Honest, but the uncertainty follows him around. His agent quietly starts taking other calls.
press.dealWaitR2: He expected better than a maybe. The performances will tell you his answer before you give him yours.
press.routQ1: {us}-{them}. A statement performance - the best this team can play, or is there more?
press.routQ2: {us}-{them}, and it barely flattered you. Where does that rank among performances in your time here?
press.routQ3: {opp} had no answers out there. {us}-{them} - is this side at its ceiling, or still climbing?
press.routMoreR: Ominous for the rest of the league. The players believe it too.
press.routMoveOnR: All business. The standard is the standard.
press.thrashQ1: {us}-{them} to {opp}. Supporters deserve an explanation. What went wrong out there?
press.thrashQ2: {us}-{them}. Some of your supporters left twenty minutes early. What do you owe them?
press.thrashQ3: A {by}-point beating. Talk us through it, because nobody in the stands could.
press.thrashOnMe: That was on me, not the players
press.thrashOnMeR: The dressing room notices who took the bullets.
press.thrashUnacceptableR: Hard words, publicly delivered. Training will be spiky this week.
press.thrashOneDayR: Calm - but the phone-ins want blood, not calm.
press.derbyWonQ1: Derby day belongs to you. The fans are singing your name outside - a message for them?
press.derbyWonQ2: You could hear your end from the tunnel. A derby won: who does it mean more to, you or them?
press.derbyWonQ3: Bragging rights are yours until the return fixture. Any words for the neighbours?
press.derbyWonEnjoyR: The clip of your grin does big numbers. Bragging rights secured.
press.derbyWonFour: It is only worth four points
press.derbyWonFourR: True, technically. Nobody outside the building agrees.
press.derbyWonCityR: Front page. Their fans will keep the receipt - mind the return fixture.
press.derbyLostQ1: A derby defeat, and their supporters are letting you know about it. How do you face your own fans this week?
press.derbyLostQ2: They will paint the town their colours tonight. A derby lost - how long does this one hurt?
press.derbyLostQ3: Your supporters filed out in silence; theirs did not. What happens now?
press.derbyLostFace: We will not hide from this
press.derbyLostFaceR: Straight talk. The fans respect honesty more than excuses.
press.derbyLostStatsR: The stats might back you up. Derby crowds do not deal in stats.
press.derbyLostReturnR: A promise. It will be remembered - deliver or else.
press.discTraining: The assistant closes the door: {player} skipped Monday's recovery session and did not think it worth an excuse. The squad knows, and the squad is watching what you do about it.
press.discForm: The assistant closes the door: {player} has been well below his own standard, and the coaches say the effort in review meetings matches the ratings. The squad knows, and the squad is watching what you do about it.
press.discWord: A quiet word, man to man
press.slotQ: The {slot_k} is on a stopgap arrangement at {weekly} a week - under the going rate. The commercial director has three offers on the desk. Which way do we go?

slotLongR.one: Signed. Safe money for {n} year - a touch under market, because the sponsor is buying certainty off you.
slotLongR.other: Signed. Safe money for {n} years - a touch under market, because the sponsor is buying certainty off you.

slotShortR.one: Signed. Over the market rate, and you are back at this desk in {n} year - which is the bet: your reputation will have grown by then.
slotShortR.other: Signed. Over the market rate, and you are back at this desk in {n} years - which is the bet: your reputation will have grown by then.

press.slotClauseR: Signed, with the clause. Deliver on the pitch and it is the best deal in the building; fall short and you sold cheap.
press.slotKeep: Stay with the stopgap for now
press.slotKeepR: The stopgap rolls on at a discount. The offers stay on the Finances screen whenever you want them.
press.refereeQ1: Two penalties in the last ten minutes, both against you, both at the breakdown. Anything you'd like to say about the officiating?
press.refereeQ2: {n} late penalties, all one way, and a game lost by a score. Was that refereed fairly?
press.refereeClips: I'll be sending the clips to the union.
press.refereeClipsR: Fined by the disciplinary panel by Wednesday. Your pack loved it. The terraces loved it more.
press.refereeOurs: Referees make decisions. We made more mistakes than he did.
press.refereeOursR: The pundits call it grown-up. The pack calls it something else, quietly, on the bus.
press.refereeUnseenR: Everyone in the room knows you have. The line dies on the table and nobody picks it up.
press.standoffQ1: {player} is out of contract in the summer and hasn't signed. Has he told you he's leaving?
press.standoffQ2: Still nothing on {player}'s new deal. Is he waiting for a better offer, or are you?
press.standoffLoved: He'll sign. He knows where he's loved.
press.standoffLovedR: Confident. {player} reads it and smiles. If he doesn't sign, this is the clip they'll run.
press.standoffBigger: Nobody is bigger than the club.
press.standoffBiggerR: Firm. His agent posts a single eyes emoji. Three clubs like it.
press.standoffBetween: That's between the player and the club.
press.standoffBetweenR: The room writes “stand-off” in inverted commas, which is worse than writing it without them.
press.weatherQ1: Forty millimetres forecast for Saturday at {opp}. You're a running side. Do you change how you play?
press.weatherQ2: It's January, it's {opp} away and the pitch is a bog. Where does the rugby go?
press.weatherKick: We'll kick it, and we'll kick it well.
press.weatherKickR: Your fly-half nods slowly. Your wingers stop listening around the word “kick”.
press.weatherSame: We play the same rugby in any weather.
press.weatherSameR: Brave. Damp. The board admires the principle from a heated box.
press.weatherCoatR: Gets a laugh. Gets printed. Gets a coat sent to the club by a local outfitter, unasked.
press.oldboyQ1: {player} faces {opp} on Saturday, his old club. Will he be starting, and will he be celebrating?
press.oldboyQ2: First time back for {player} against {opp}. How do you handle a man playing his old mates?
press.oldboyCelebrate: He'll start, and he can celebrate how he likes.
press.oldboyCelebrateR: He scores. He celebrates. Their end remembers it, and so does yours.
press.oldboyBehaveR: He behaves. He also has his quietest game of the season, which may be related.
press.oldboyFridayR: You have never once announced a team on a Friday, and the room knows it.
press.kidstartQ1: {player} is nineteen and starting at {pos_k} against a side that will know it. Brave or reckless?
press.kidstartQ2: A first start for {player} at nineteen. What does he know at kick-off that he didn't know this morning?
press.kidstartReadyR: He's ready. His mother is not. {senior} watches from the bench with an expression.
press.kidstartInjuries: We've got injuries. He's what we have.
press.kidstartInjuriesR: Honest. He reads it. He plays like a man who has read it.
press.kidstartFirstR: Warm, and true, and he plays like it - like a man having a first game.
press.seatsQ1: {n} empty seats on Saturday. Are the supporters telling you something?
press.seatsQ2: Three home games, three half-empty stands. Whose fault is that?
press.seatsListeningR: The supporters' trust invites you to their AGM. You go. Upstairs would rather you hadn't admitted anything.
press.seatsPricesR: The commercial director's department reads that before you've left the room.
press.seatsWinR: They do, eventually. Nobody has ever said “eventually” in a press conference and enjoyed it.
press.leakQ1: We're hearing {player} has been dropped for Saturday - before you've told him. Who's talking in your dressing room?
press.leakQ2: {player}'s name was on a team sheet in a pub last night, and not the one you've handed in. Where's the leak?
press.leakLong: Somebody who won't be in it for long.
press.leakLongR: Menacing. Nobody confesses. Three people stop talking to each other, and one of them is innocent.
press.leakStarts: You've got it wrong. He starts.
press.leakStartsR: You now have to start {player}. He knows it. So does the man he replaces.
press.leakTalkR: A shrug. The leaker leaks again by Thursday, encouraged.
press.centuryQ1: {player}'s {what_k} on Saturday. Is he the best you've worked with?
press.centuryQ2: A {what_k} for {player}. What does he mean to this place?
press.centuryBestR: He's told. Twice. By his mates. {captain_k}
press.centuryCaptainSulks: {captain} hears it too, and says nothing, pointedly.
press.centuryConversationR: Diplomatic. He noticed the word “conversation” and will mention it at Christmas.
press.centuryTwoHundred: Ask me after he's got to two hundred.
press.centuryTwoHundredR: A laugh, and a target. He has a hundred to go and has already started counting.

benchQ1.one: {player} hasn't started in a week. His agent says he's “exploring options”. Are you?
benchQ1.other: {player} hasn't started in {n} weeks. His agent says he's “exploring options”. Are you?

benchQ2.one: A week on the bench for {player}, and he is better than that. What has he done?
benchQ2.other: {n} weeks on the bench for {player}, and he is better than that. What has he done?

press.benchDoor: He can explore. My door's open.
press.benchDoorR: It is. He walks through it on Monday with a transfer request and a printout.
press.benchBuilding: He's a big part of what we're building.
press.benchBuildingR: He has read that sentence before, in two other programmes, about two other men.
press.benchNextWeekR: {player} starts next week. You have just picked your team in a press conference.
press.comebackQ1: Down by {n} at the break. What on earth did you say at half time?
press.comebackQ2: Fifteen behind and out. Then not. Talk us through the dressing room at half time.
press.comebackCaptain: Nothing. I let the captain speak.
press.comebackCaptainR: {captain} becomes a folk hero by teatime. You become “the quiet one”, which you can live with.
press.comebackTruthR: Which was, according to a source in the room, quite loud and mostly accurate.
press.comebackRoomR: Everyone respects it. Everyone tries to find out. Somebody will, by Wednesday.
press.homeQ1: {player} has not looked himself since the move. His family are still in {home_k} and the word around the club is that he is finding it hard. Is he homesick?
press.homeQ2: There is a story going round that {player} is struggling to settle - new country, new league, and {home_k} a long way off. Anything in it?
press.homeQ3: {player} moved a long way to come here and has looked flat for weeks. Is this about rugby, or is it about home?
press.homeSettle: We will help him build a life here
press.homeSettleR: Warm, and specific enough to be believed. {player} reads it twice, and somebody at the club spends Thursday helping his family find a school.
press.homeProfessional: Every professional moves. He knew that
press.homeProfessionalR: True, and cold, and the whole dressing room hears the temperature. {player} nods along in front of the cameras and rings his agent that night.
press.homeSenior: One of the senior lads has taken him under his wing
press.homeSeniorR: The room likes that answer. {player} has somewhere to be on a Sunday now, which is worth more than a team talk.
press.weightQ1: {player} is {age} and has played nearly every week. He looked short of confidence on Saturday. Is the weight of it getting to him?
press.weightQ2: At {age}, {player} has had a lot asked of him this season and the form has gone. Have you leaned on him too hard?
press.weightQ3: {player} is {age} years old and carrying a lot for a side that needs him. Is that fair on the boy?
press.weightMine: The pressure is mine, not his
press.weightMineR: You take it off him in public, which is the only place it can be taken off. {player} plays the next one like a man with nothing to lose.
press.weightSignedUp: This is the job. He signed up for it
press.weightSignedUpR: Hard, and some of the old pros agree with you. {player} is not one of them, and the next few weeks will say whether it worked.
press.weightRest: He will get a week out of the firing line
press.weightRestR: A quiet answer that costs you nothing and gives him a Saturday to breathe. He will be better for it, if you actually give him the week.
press.baroDealQ1: {player} is out of contract soon and there is still no news of a new deal. Is there a problem?
press.baroDealQ2: The talks over a new contract for {player} have gone quiet. Should supporters be worried?
press.baroDealPrivate: Talks are private, and they are going well
press.baroDealPrivateR: The room wanted a crack and you gave them a closed door. {player} appreciates it, and the pack leave with nothing.
press.baroDealPriceR: Tomorrow's headline writes itself. The pack are delighted with you; the dressing room reads it as a For Sale sign.
press.baroBite: You want a story because we keep winning
press.baroBiteR: The supporters love it and the squad laugh along. The pack do not, and they will remember who made them look silly.
press.baroDealSaturday: I will talk about Saturday, not contracts
press.baroDealSaturdayR: Nothing to write and nothing to regret. The pack move on to the next question.
press.baroSuitorQ1: Word is {club} are watching {player}. Can you keep hold of your best players while this side is winning?
press.baroSuitorQ2: {club} are said to be ready to make a move for {player}. Is anyone at this club for sale?
press.baroSuitorNo: Nobody is for sale, and certainly not {player}
press.baroSuitorNoR: A clear answer. {player} hears it, the supporters cheer it, and the pack have to find their story somewhere else.
press.baroSuitorListen: If the offer is right, we will always listen
press.baroSuitorListenR: Honest, and the board appreciate it. The dressing room hears that nobody is safe, which was exactly the point of the question.
press.baroSuitorNoCall: Nobody has called me, so there is nothing to say
press.baroSuitorNoCallR: A straight answer. It calms the story down, even if it does not kill it.
press.baroRowQ1: {player} is said to be unhappy about being left out. Is there a row in the camp?
press.baroRowQ2: We hear there were words at training over selection, and the name {player} keeps coming up. What happened?
press.baroRowNone: No row. Everyone here wants to play, which is how it should be
press.baroRowNoneR: You close it down without shutting anyone out. The squad like that, and the pack find little to chew on.
press.baroRowTrain: If anyone wants a shirt, the answer is to train harder
press.baroRowTrainR: The pack have their line. {player} has just been told off in public, and will not forget it quickly.
press.baroRowGuess: Whoever told you that is guessing
press.baroRowGuessR: A shot back at the room, and the supporters enjoy it. The pack take it personally.
press.baroRowPrivate: Selection stays in the dressing room
press.baroRowPrivateR: Fair enough, the pack concede. The story goes no further this week.
press.baroSmugQ1: {n} wins in a row. Is the squad starting to believe its own headlines?
press.baroSmugQ2: {n} straight wins, and the only thing that can stop this side now is complacency. Is that the danger?
press.baroSmugHungry: This group is far too hungry for that
press.baroSmugHungryR: The squad hear their manager backing them and walk a little taller. The pack wanted a worry and did not get one.
press.baroSmugNothingR: Grounded and sensible. The board like it, the pack respect it, and one or two in the squad wish you had enjoyed it more.
press.baroAllTheWay: This side can go all the way
press.baroAllTheWayR: The headline writes itself and the supporters buy every word. The pack will write the other story just as happily if it goes wrong, and now they will be looking for it.
press.baroSmugMay: Ask me again at the end of the season
press.baroSmugMayR: A smile and a shrug. The pack get a quote and the supporters get a line to repeat.
press.baroHostileQ1: The results say this side is going backwards. How long do you think the board will give you?
press.baroHostileQ2: There are people outside this room saying the job is too big for you. What do you say to them?
press.baroHostileQ3: Supporters are asking whether this squad has stopped playing for you. Has it?
press.baroDefend: They are giving everything. Judge me, not them
press.baroDefendR: The dressing room hears it. The pack wanted someone to blame and you did not give them anyone, which they do not enjoy.
press.baroOnMe: The results are not good enough, and that is on me
press.baroOnMeR: Honest, and the room respects honesty. The pack ease off, for a week at least.
press.baroNextGame: I am only thinking about the next game
press.baroNextGameR: Nothing to quote, which calms things down more than anything clever would have.
press.baroWroteOff: Some of you wrote us off before a ball was kicked. You were wrong then too
press.baroWroteOffR: The terraces love it and the clip is everywhere by lunchtime. The pack do not forgive being made to look foolish.
press.baroBlame: Some of the squad need to take a hard look at themselves
press.baroBlameR: The pack have their headline. The dressing room has a manager who went public on them, and that is hard to take back.
press.baroScepticQ1: A couple of poor results and the questions have started. Is this a blip or something more?
press.baroScepticQ2: The side looks short of ideas at the moment. What is going wrong?
press.baroWarmQ1: Everyone is talking about the way this side is playing. How much of the credit is yours?
press.baroWarmQ2: The supporters are dreaming again. How far can this team go?
press.baroWarmQ3: It has been a good few weeks. What has changed?
press.baroWarmPlayers: All of it belongs to the squad
press.baroWarmPlayersR: Generous, and the squad notice. The pack like a manager who shares it round.
press.baroWarmFansR: The terraces hear it and sing it back on Saturday. The pack print it gladly.
press.baroWarmFeet: Feet on the ground. We have won nothing
press.baroWarmFeetR: Sensible, and a little dull for the back pages. The board like it; the pack were hoping for more.
press.banAcceptR_f: No circus, no lawyers. The panel notes the club's professionalism, and the player serves her time quietly.
press.finalTrapR_f: You talk the week down to protect the group. Sensible - though one or two of the younger players wanted to hear the fire.
press.hotQ1_f: {player} has been in scintillating form - some are calling her the best {pos_k} in the competition. Do you agree?
press.hotFeet_f: Keep her feet on the ground
press.hotOthersR_f: You spread the praise across the whole side. {player} nods along, and the pack notes the mention of the women who win her ball.
press.coldQ1_f: {player} has looked well short of her best in recent weeks. Is her place under threat?
press.coldQ2_f: Be honest about {player} - the supporters on the message boards already are. What is going wrong for her?
press.coldQ3_f: {player} would struggle to make most sides in this league on current form. Does she keep the shirt?
press.coldBlameR_f: “If she is short of form, look at how I am using her.” The room did not expect that. {player} did not either, and she trains like a woman with a debt to repay.
press.rumourAsk_f: Ask her - she is happy here
press.kidQ1_f: Everyone is talking about {player} - {age} years old and lighting up the league. Is she the future of the club?
press.kidQ2_f: {player}, {age}, and already the first name the supporters sing. How good can she actually be?
press.kidCrownR_f: {player} floats out of the press room - and every scout in the hemisphere just circled her name.
press.kidProtectR_f: Measured. She keeps developing away from the circus.
press.kidEarn_f: She plays when she earns it
press.unveilQ1_f: {player} is in the room for her unveiling, shirt in hand. What are you expecting from your new {pos_k}?
press.unveilQ2_f: New shirt, new number, cameras everywhere: {player} is officially yours. What did you sign her to do?
press.unveilMarqueeR_f: “She changes everything for us.” {player} beams - and every match report this season will measure her against that sentence.
press.unveilSettleR_f: Sensible. The pressure valve stays closed while she learns the calls.
press.unveilFightR_f: A cold shower at her own unveiling. The squad notes that nobody gets given a shirt here.
press.intlFringeR_f: Ten women who train all week and watch all weekend just sat up straighter.
press.plansQ1_f: {player} knocks and closes the door behind her. “Boss, I have barely played all season. Tell me straight - am I in your plans or not?”
press.plansInR1_f: {player} leaves with her head up. She will hold you to it - pick her soon or this conversation happens again, louder.
press.plansInR2_f: The tension goes out of her shoulders. A promise in this office is a promise on the team sheet, she will be counting the weeks.
press.plansOut_f: Honestly? She can find a new club
press.plansOutR1_f: A hard truth, kindly delivered. {player} thanks you for being straight, and her agent is making calls within the hour.
press.plansOutR2_f: She goes quiet, then nods. “Appreciate the honesty, boss.” The listing will not shock anyone in the dressing room.
press.plansEarnR1_f: She nods, jaw tight, and heads back to training. The squad hears about it, the honest ones respect it.
press.plansEarnR2_f: “Fine. Then I will take one.” She trains like a woman possessed all week. That answer either made her or lost her.
press.loanQ3_f: The academy coach sends {player} up to see you. The kid gets it out in one breath: “Loan me out, boss. I will come back better - or I will come back and you can tell me I was wrong.”
press.loanMinutesR1_f: {player} lights up. Play her in the next few weeks or the shine wears off fast.
press.loanMinutesR2_f: She floats out of the office. A first-team promise at her age is rocket fuel - but it burns fast if the team sheet never shows it.
press.loanAgreeR2_f: She grins and shakes your hand twice, and the academy coach makes the calls before you have changed your mind: minutes make players, benches make excuses.
press.loanStay_f: She is not ready to leave
press.loanStayR1_f: She trudges out without a word. The academy coach thinks you have just cooled your hottest prospect.
press.loanStayR2_f: “Right.” One word, and the door does not slam, which is somehow worse. Keep an eye on her training reports.
press.dealYearR1_f: {player} shakes your hand hard. Offer the terms from her player page before someone else does.
press.dealYearR2_f: Relief, then a grin you have not seen since pre-season. Get the paperwork moving before her agent hears anything else.
press.dealLast_f: This season is her last here
press.dealLastR1_f: She takes it with dignity. She will finish the job properly - and the young players just saw how endings are handled here.
press.dealWaitR1_f: Honest, but the uncertainty follows her around. Her agent quietly starts taking other calls.
press.dealWaitR2_f: She expected better than a maybe. The performances will tell you her answer before you give her yours.
press.discForm_f: The assistant closes the door: {player} has been well below her own standard, and the coaches say the effort in review meetings matches the ratings. The squad knows, and the squad is watching what you do about it.
press.discWord_f: A quiet word, face to face
press.standoffQ1_f: {player} is out of contract in the summer and hasn't signed. Has she told you she's leaving?
press.standoffQ2_f: Still nothing on {player}'s new deal. Is she waiting for a better offer, or are you?
press.standoffLoved_f: She'll sign. She knows where she's loved.
press.standoffLovedR_f: Confident. {player} reads it and smiles. If she doesn't sign, this is the clip they'll run.
press.standoffBiggerR_f: Firm. Her agent posts a single eyes emoji. Three clubs like it.
press.oldboyQ1_f: {player} faces {opp} on Saturday, her old club. Will she be starting, and will she be celebrating?
press.oldboyQ2_f: First time back for {player} against {opp}. How do you handle a woman playing her old mates?
press.oldboyCelebrate_f: She'll start, and she can celebrate how she likes.
press.oldboyCelebrateR_f: She scores. She celebrates. Their end remembers it, and so does yours.
press.oldboyBehaveR_f: She behaves. She also has her quietest game of the season, which may be related.
press.kidstartQ2_f: A first start for {player} at nineteen. What does she know at kick-off that she didn't know this morning?
press.kidstartReadyR_f: She's ready. Her mother is not. {senior} watches from the bench with an expression.
press.kidstartInjuries_f: We've got injuries. She's what we have.
press.kidstartInjuriesR_f: Honest. She reads it. She plays like a woman who has read it.
press.kidstartFirstR_f: Warm, and true, and she plays like it - like a woman having a first game.
press.leakQ1_f: We're hearing {player} has been dropped for Saturday - before you've told her. Who's talking in your dressing room?
press.leakStarts_f: You've got it wrong. She starts.
press.leakStartsR_f: You now have to start {player}. She knows it. So does the woman she replaces.
press.centuryQ1_f: {player}'s {what_k} on Saturday. Is she the best you've worked with?
press.centuryQ2_f: A {what_k} for {player}. What does she mean to this place?
press.centuryBestR_f: She's told. Twice. By her mates. {captain_k}
press.centuryConversationR_f: Diplomatic. She noticed the word “conversation” and will mention it at Christmas.
press.centuryTwoHundred_f: Ask me after she's got to two hundred.
press.centuryTwoHundredR_f: A laugh, and a target. She has a hundred to go and has already started counting.

benchQ1_f.one: {player} hasn't started in a week. Her agent says she's “exploring options”. Are you?
benchQ1_f.other: {player} hasn't started in {n} weeks. Her agent says she's “exploring options”. Are you?

benchQ2_f.one: A week on the bench for {player}, and she is better than that. What has she done?
benchQ2_f.other: {n} weeks on the bench for {player}, and she is better than that. What has she done?

press.benchDoor_f: She can explore. My door's open.
press.benchDoorR_f: It is. She walks through it on Monday with a transfer request and a printout.
press.benchBuilding_f: She's a big part of what we're building.
press.benchBuildingR_f: She has read that sentence before, in two other programmes, about two other women.
press.homeQ1_f: {player} has not looked herself since the move. Her family are still in {home_k} and the word around the club is that she is finding it hard. Is she homesick?
press.homeSettleR_f: Warm, and specific enough to be believed. {player} reads it twice, and somebody at the club spends Thursday helping her family find a school.
press.homeProfessionalR_f: True, and cold, and the whole dressing room hears the temperature. {player} nods along in front of the cameras and rings her agent that night.
press.homeSenior_f: One of the senior girls has taken her under her wing
press.weightQ1_f: {player} is {age} and has played nearly every week. She looked short of confidence on Saturday. Is the weight of it getting to her?
press.weightQ2_f: At {age}, {player} has had a lot asked of her this season and the form has gone. Have you leaned on her too hard?
press.weightQ3_f: {player} is {age} years old and carrying a lot for a side that needs her. Is that fair on the girl?
press.weightMineR_f: You take it off her in public, which is the only place it can be taken off. {player} plays the next one like a woman with nothing to lose.
press.stanceSafeR_w: You talk the year down to take the heat off the group. The boardroom needle is muted both ways: defeats cost less, but so does winning - credit is thin for a woman who promised nothing.{tail_k}
press.raceQ1_w: The title race is down to you and {club}. {coach_k} says her side “handles the big moments better”. Care to respond?
press.raceQ2_w: {coach_k} lit the fuse this morning: her {short} side “handles the big moments better”, apparently. Your reply?
press.ownerRugbyR_w: Confident, direct - owners like a woman who volunteers for the scoreboard.
press.discWord_w: A quiet word, woman to woman
press.acadFirstQ: The academy director, on {player} ({pos}, {age}): a first year done. Offer a development contract, or release now? The director's advice: {adv_k}
press.acadGateQ: The academy director, on {player} ({pos}, {age}): the development deal ends at 21, this summer. A first professional contract, or release? The director's advice: {adv_k}
press.acadAdviceSign: sign. The ceiling is good enough for this squad one day.
press.acadAdvicePromote: offer the contract. Close enough to the first team to be worth the wage.
press.acadAdviceRelease: release. The ceiling falls short of this squad.
press.acadSignR: Done. {player} signs on and stays in the academy.
press.acadPromoteR: Done. {player} signs a professional contract and joins the first-team squad.
press.acadReleaseR: {player} leaves the academy as a free agent, with the club's thanks.

till.boardBlurb: Real money through the app store, signed into this save with no way back.
till.injWage: The board underwrites {weekly} of wages outside the cap until summer.
till.injNone: The owners will not go to the well again this year.
till.xlWait: The Sugar Daddy calls once a day. Ready again in about {h}h.
till.injLanded: The funds have landed: {amount} added to the budget and the books.
till.injHeld: Paid, and held: the board will not vote it through again this season. It stays yours - this page will offer it again when the well refills.
till.pending: The store is still processing it. Nothing more to do - when it lands, this page will offer it to the career in front of you.
till.charterBody: The league's salary cap stops applying to this club. No ceiling, no fines, no embargoes - permanent, this save only, and the save wears the mark.
till.charterConfirm: Remove it - there is no way back
till.charterDone: Done. The wage law no longer applies to this club.
till.charterSigned: The cap is gone for as long as this career runs: no ceiling, no fines, no embargoes.
till.charterOwned: You own this. Turn it on below when you are certain - it cannot be turned off.
till.fineprint: Prices are the store's own. A purchase is only spent once it has landed in your career; if anything is interrupted, this page offers it back.
till.watchAgency: Ask the agency for their file (watch a spot)
till.analystDone: The analyst's full read is on the card - the briefing above is the whole of it.
till.townBody: The supporters' trust will pass the bucket for a club in real trouble - watch a spot and the collection lands in the bank. It pays wages and lights, never players.
till.townDone: The collection came to {amount}. It is in the bank.
till.agencyDone: The agency's file on {name} is in: every attribute, and the character to go with it.
till.spotSkipped: The spot was closed early, so nothing changed - the favour needs the whole thing.
till.spotUnavailable: No spot is available right now. Nothing is lost - try again later.
till.favourGone: The moment has passed: the week's allowance was already used.

watchAnalyst.one: The analyst has one more read - his all-nighter for a spot
watchAnalyst.other: The analyst has {n} more reads - his all-nighter for a spot

till.owedHeld: Already paid for. It has not been delivered yet, so you have not been charged again - the game keeps trying in the background. Come back in a minute.

watchAnalyst_w.one: The analyst has one more read - her all-nighter for a spot
watchAnalyst_w.other: The analyst has {n} more reads - her all-nighter for a spot

till.insideDone: The agent's inside word on {name} is in: the rival-interest line now reads as the full file would read it.
till.opinionDone: A second opinion on {name} is in: the staff's estimate of the ceiling is a step narrower for the rest of the season.
till.watchTeamNight: Stand by it, and the sponsor stands the squad a team night (watch a spot)
till.teamNightDone: The sponsor's team night took some of the sting out of it for the senior players.

store.title: Store
store.bought: Yours. It follows your store account - Restore brings it back on a new phone.
store.needCareer: Open a career first - the retreat needs a squad to visit.
store.removeAdsLine: No adverts, ever. Three skins only Pro managers get. Nothing about the rugby changes.
store.removeAdsLineSkins: Three skins only Pro managers get. Nothing about the rugby changes.
store.healLine: Every injury healed, the whole squad fresh. Once per club match played.
store.healDone: Done: the whole squad reports fit.
store.healNobody: Paid, and held: there is nobody to mend right now. It stays yours - apply it when it counts.
store.creditGone: Nothing left to apply here. If the store refunded an older purchase, it can simply be bought again.
store.healWait: The retreat needs a match between visits - play one and it reopens.
store.pinnacleLine: Take charge of an international side alongside your club. Pick the country and you are their head coach on the spot.
store.callMade: Appointed: you are the head coach of {nat}. Your Manager Profile asks the one thing left - do you carry on at the club?
store.callRefused: Not now: you already hold a national job, a federation matter is open, or this career has had its call.
store.estateLine: Every facility to its maximum, for the club that builds it.
store.estateConfirm: Build it - the whole estate, for good
store.estateDone: Done. Nine world-class facilities, and the running costs to match.
store.estateRefused: Nothing to build: the estate is already at its ceiling.
store.charterLine: No wage ceiling, ever again, on the save that turns it on.
store.fundingLine: Four board resolutions, £10m to £130m, each with a season of cap-exempt wages.
store.fineprint: One-off payments, handled by the app store. Nothing here plays the matches, and the game still sends nothing about you anywhere.
store.tillSilent: The store is connected but has not answered yet. Buying can still work - its own sheet opens before anything is charged. If this build just arrived, give it a minute.
store.tillPartial: The store answered for {live} of {asked} products. The others may not be on sale to this account yet.
store.pickNation: Yours. Pick the federation and take the job - the appointment is immediate.
store.supportLine: A thank-you to the developer. It changes nothing in the game.

supportThanks.one: Put in once. Thank you - it genuinely matters.
supportThanks.other: Put in {n} times. Thank you - it genuinely matters.

store.supportDone: Thank you. That is {n} from you now, and it goes straight back into the game.
store.charterRefused: Not here: this career has no cap left to lift, or there is no club on the desk.
store.estateAgain: The buildings stayed at your old club. This ground starts again.
store.healNext: Used this round. Available again after your next match.

settings.title: Settings
settings.sub: How the game looks, not how it plays
settings.skinLine: Every screen, repainted. The Clubhouse green is everyone's; the other three come with Pro Manager. Nothing about the rugby changes either way.
settings.skinProCta: Get the other three with Pro Manager
settings.skinDefaultLine: The green and gold the game was built in.
settings.skinMidnightLine: Navy and electric cyan. The gantry view, all telestrator and no tea urn.
settings.skinHeritageLine: Oatmeal and deep burgundy. Reads like a Sunday broadsheet that still calls it rugby football.
settings.skinStealthLine: True black and one clean accent. Nothing on screen but the numbers.
settings.floodOn: They are on - the dark ground, which is how most people play.
settings.floodOff: They are off - daylight, for reading in the sun.
settings.langLine: The whole game, not just the menus.
settings.pronounLine: How the papers, the fans and the board refer to you. Change it whenever you like.
settings.textSizeLine: Bigger type, same game - every screen still fits the phone.
settings.fineprint: The colours, the light and the type size live on this phone, not in the save - a career carried to another device arrives in that one's colours. How the press refer to you goes with the career. Currently reading in {lang}.
settings.introLine: The five-second intro when the game starts. A tap skips it.

sack.head: You are out at {club}
sack.ask: The cameras are already outside. You have to say something.
sack.ownedLine: I deserved it. You do not lose that many and get to blame the fixture list. The players gave me everything, the results were mine, and the club is right to want better.
sack.ownedReply: It leads every bulletin by six o'clock. Nobody has a follow-up question, which is its own kind of verdict - and one old pro on the panel says he would have you at his club tomorrow.
sack.spiteLine: Honestly? I did not like the team anyway. Bad squad, worse canteen, and a training pitch a farmer would apologise for. Somebody will win something there in about nine years.
sack.spiteReply: It is a clip before you reach the car park. The supporters' forum has forty pages on it by tea time and somebody has already made the canteen line into a flag.
sack.unfairLine: It was unfair, and everyone in this room knows it. Injuries all winter, no money in January, and eleven weeks to fix what took ten years to break. Judge me on a full season or do not judge me at all.
sack.unfairReply: Half the room writes "dignified", the other half writes "excuses". Both pieces run. That is the press for you - you were never going to get one headline out of this.

isles.title: The Isles XV
isles.whyNoTour: There is no tour this summer. They go once every four years.
isles.whyNoJob: You would need a job first.
isles.whyNotIntl: The four unions choose from coaches already running one of their own national sides.
isles.whyNoTrophy: They pick coaches who have won something. You have not, yet.
isles.whyRep: Your standing in the game is not yet what this job asks for. Nothing else in rugby asks for as much.
isles.whyYes: You meet every condition the four unions set.
isles.took: You are the head coach of the British & Irish Isles XV. Your assistant has your country until you are home.
isles.passed: You told them no. They will ask somebody else, and they will not ask you again this time.

close.title: The summer diary
close.sub: No rugby. The ground still earns.
close.weddingD: The function room, a marquee and a Saturday. Small, steady, and nobody touches the pitch.
close.comedyD: A name off the telly and 300 seats in the clubhouse. Cheap to put on.
close.townshowD: The town on your grass for a weekend. Needs room, and the grounds staff will want a word after.
close.golfD: A day out for people who might sponsor you. Pays in goodwill and in cash.
close.shootingD: Clays, a cold morning and a bacon roll. The same crowd as the golf day, and rather more of them than you expected.
close.sponsorD: Black tie, a raffle and the people who pay for your shirt. The best room in the building earns its keep.
close.concertD: Twenty thousand on the pitch in July. The best cheque of the summer, and it wrecks the grass - the re-turfing comes out of the fee.
close.locked: Your ground cannot hold this one yet
close.notNow: The season is on. The diary opens when the rugby stops.
close.alreadyBooked: Something is already in the diary that week. It is one ground.
close.cannotHost: Your ground cannot hold that one yet.

close.mishapGolf: two buggies in the pond and a green to re-seed
close.mishapShooting: an insurance excess after a very near miss
close.mishapSponsor: the caterer's invoice came in well over the quote
close.mishapConcert: the stage rig took out a section of terrace
