point.ticketsSubj: The board has seen the gate figures
point.tickets:
{stadium} has been {pct}% full this season and the board has put the number in front of you rather than in a report. Nobody has said the word "crisis" - they have said "footfall", twice, which is worse.

Winning fixes this faster than any marketing plan. They know that. They would still like to hear a plan.
point.advertSubj: The campaign has gone viral. Not like that.
point.advert:
The new season campaign was shot in a wind tunnel with a slogan nobody read aloud first. It has been viewed several million times this week, almost none of them kindly, and the sponsor has extended for {fee} on the strength of it.

The commercial director is delighted. The supporters are not. Both of those are going to stay true for a while.
point.awaykitSubj: The away kit has been unveiled
point.awaykit:
{club} launched the new away shirt this week. The design team called it "heritage-inspired". The forum called it several other things, at length, with pictures.

It has also sold {fee} worth in four days and the shop cannot keep it in stock. Nobody at the club is pretending to understand it either.
point.breakaway:
A consortium nobody can name has briefed three newspapers about a new competition: bigger money, fewer clubs, a franchise model, and an invitation your board is said to be "considering carefully".

Your chairman has said nothing publicly. The players have read it on their phones like everyone else.
point.breakawayEnd:
The consortium has stopped returning calls. Two of the newspapers have quietly moved on and the third is running a piece about how it was never really going to happen.

It never is. It comes round every few years, it fills a fortnight of back pages, and then everybody plays on Saturday as though nobody had ever mentioned it.
point.leak:
A rival coach has been unusually generous with a journalist this week - how your team lines up from a set piece, who makes the calls, which side of the field you go to first. It is in print with no name attached and far too much detail to have come from a supporter.

Whoever you play next has read it. Nothing to be done about it now but play.

board.roomSub: four asks, and none of them cheap
board.askDesc_time: A public backing from the chairman. It does not win matches; it buys you the weeks to.
board.askDesc_funds: A top-up to the transfer budget, out of the club's own reserves.
board.askDesc_facilities: The board pays for the next build outright, rather than letting you spend for it.
board.ask_staff: Ask for a bigger staff budget
board.askDesc_staff: A fund ring-fenced for the backroom: coaches, courses, and moving someone on.
board.blockEstateMax: Nothing left to build. Every facility is already world class.
board.blockBuilders: The builders are already on site. One project at a time.
board.blockNotStruggling: You are not under pressure. Asking for time you do not need would create some.
board.blockAlreadyTime: The chairman has already backed you publicly. Use it.
board.blockFundsSeason: You have already been to them for money this season.
board.blockStaffSeason: You have already been to them for the backroom this season.
board.caseThin: You would be asking on very little.
board.caseShut: They said no recently. Asking again is pressing them.

talk.plansInGood: {player} stands a little taller. “That's all I needed to hear, boss. I'll be ready.”
talk.plansInMixed: {player} nods, not quite convinced. “Words are easy. Put my name on the sheet and I'll believe it.”
talk.plansInBad: {player} laughs without smiling. “Everyone says that. I've heard it at three clubs.”
talk.plansOutGood: {player} takes a breath. “Thank you for being straight. I'd rather know.”
talk.plansOutMixed: {player} goes quiet for a moment. “Fair enough. At least I know where I stand. My agent will be in touch.”
talk.plansOutBad: {player} stands up too fast for the chair. “After everything I've given this club? Right. Noted.”
talk.plansEarnGood: {player} grins. “Challenge accepted. Watch me in training this week.”
talk.plansEarnMixed: {player} shrugs. “I've been earning it all season. Not sure what else there is to show.”
talk.plansEarnBad: {player} stares at the floor. “Earn it how, from the stand? That's a brush-off and we both know it.”
talk.loanMinutesGood: {player} lights up. “Minutes here? Even better. I won't let you down.”
talk.loanMinutesMixed: {player} hesitates. “If they come, great. I'll give it until the new year.”
talk.loanMinutesBad: {player} folds both arms. “I've heard about minutes before. I'd rather have the loan.”
talk.loanAgreeGood: {player} shakes your hand twice. “Thank you, boss. I'll come back better.”
talk.loanAgreeMixed: {player} manages a smile. “Right. I didn't think you'd actually say yes. I'll go and pack.”
talk.loanAgreeBad: {player} goes pale. “Oh. I thought you'd fight to keep me.”
talk.loanStayGood: {player} nods slowly. “Okay. If you think I'm needed here, I'll stay and work.”
talk.loanStayMixed: {player} sighs. “I'll stay. But I'm not getting any younger on that bench.”
talk.loanStayBad: {player} is already at the door. “Then I'll find someone who does think I'm ready.”
talk.dealYearGood: {player} lets out a long breath. “One more year. I'll make it count, boss.”
talk.dealYearMixed: {player} weighs it up. “A year's a start. We'll talk numbers, though.”
talk.dealYearBad: {player} frowns. “Just the one? I was hoping this place thought more of me.”
talk.dealLastGood: {player} nods. “Thank you for telling me now. Let's make it a good last season.”
talk.dealLastMixed: {player} looks out of the window. “I suppose I'd better start ringing round.”
talk.dealLastBad: {player} can hardly get the words out. “That's it, then. Nobody even asked if I was finished.”
talk.dealWaitGood: {player} shrugs it off. “Fair. Let the run-in decide. I'm not worried.”
talk.dealWaitMixed: {player} doesn't love it. “Okay. But other clubs won't wait until May.”
talk.dealWaitBad: {player} bristles. “So I'm auditioning, at my age? Brilliant.”
talk.droppedQ1: {player} is waiting outside the office after the team meeting. “Two weeks in the stand, boss. I'd like to know why.”
talk.droppedQ2: {player} closes the office door. “I started most of this season. Now I'm not even on the bench. What changed?”
talk.droppedForm: Your form dipped. Win the shirt back in training
talk.droppedBack: It was tactical. You'll be back next week
talk.droppedFinal: It's my decision and it's not up for debate
talk.droppedFormGood: {player} nods firmly. “Fair. I'll be the first one out on the training pitch tomorrow.”
talk.droppedFormMixed: {player} isn't sure. “My form's fine. But okay, I'll show you again.”
talk.droppedFormBad: {player} scoffs. “My form? Look at the numbers. This isn't about form.”
talk.droppedBackGood: {player} relaxes. “That's all I wanted to hear. Thanks, boss.”
talk.droppedBackMixed: {player} raises an eyebrow. “Next week, then. I'll be checking the sheet.”
talk.droppedBackBad: {player} isn't buying it. “Tactical, two weeks running? Right.”
talk.droppedYouthGood: {player} takes it on the chin. “Then I'll help bring the youngster on. That's how it should work.”
talk.droppedYouthMixed: {player} goes quiet. “So that's how it is. I thought I had a few years left.”
talk.droppedYouthBad: {player} is on their feet. “I'm not done. And if you think I am, I'll go somewhere that doesn't.”
talk.droppedFinalGood: {player} half smiles. “Fair enough. You're the boss.”
talk.droppedFinalMixed: {player} nods stiffly. “Understood.” The door closes a little harder than it opened.
talk.droppedFinalBad: {player} leaves without a word. By lunchtime half the dressing room knows how that went.
talk.signingQ1: Your captain {player} catches you after training. “The lads have seen the news about {signing}. {rival} in particular is asking where that leaves them. What do I tell the room?”
talk.signingQ2: {player} knocks as captain, not as a friend. “Signing {signing} has put a few noses out of joint, {rival} most of all. The room wants to hear it from you.”
talk.signingReassure: Nobody has lost their place. Everyone has to keep it
talk.signingCompete: Competition makes us better. That's the point
talk.signingHelp: I need you to make the new player feel welcome
talk.signingMine: Selection is my job, not the dressing room's
talk.signingReassureGood: {player} looks relieved. “That's the right message. I'll pass it on word for word.”
talk.signingReassureMixed: {player} nods. “I'll tell them. Not sure {rival} will believe it until the team sheet goes up.”
talk.signingReassureBad: {player} isn't convinced. “They'll hear that as spin. So do I, a bit.”
talk.signingCompeteGood: {player} likes it. “Good. A bit of edge in training never hurt anyone.”
talk.signingCompeteMixed: {player} tilts a hand. “Fine. Just don't lose {rival} over it.”
talk.signingCompeteBad: {player} bristles. “Easy to say when it isn't your shirt on the line.”
talk.signingHelpGood: {player} is already on it. “Leave it with me. {signing} will be one of us by Friday.”
talk.signingHelpMixed: {player} sighs. “I'll do it. Would have been nice to be asked before the signing, mind.”
talk.signingHelpBad: {player} folds both arms. “I'm the captain, not the welcome committee.”
talk.signingMineGood: {player} nods. “Fair. I'll tell them to get on with it.”
talk.signingMineMixed: {player} pauses. “Understood. I'll keep a lid on it, but they won't like it.”
talk.signingMineBad: {player} goes cold. “Then don't ask me to manage the room for you.” The mood at training says the room heard.
talk.armbandQ1: {player} asks for five minutes. “I'll just say it, boss: I want to captain this side. I think I'd do it well.”
talk.armbandQ2: {player} has clearly rehearsed this. “{captain} does a good job with the armband. I'd do a better one. I'd like the chance.”
talk.armbandYes: It's yours. You're my new captain
talk.armbandEarn: Lead without it first. Then we'll talk
talk.armbandYesGood: {player} shakes your hand. “You won't regret it.” Word travels fast: the room has a new captain.
talk.armbandYesMixed: {player} is pleased, and a little surprised. “Right. I'd better get this right, then.”
talk.armbandYesBad: {player} takes it, but uneasily. “I just hope the room sees it the way you do.”
talk.armbandViceGood: {player} smiles. “That'll do me. I'll learn the job properly.”
talk.armbandViceMixed: {player} nods. “It's a step. Not the one I asked for, but a step.”
talk.armbandViceBad: {player} is polite about it. “Vice. Right.” The disappointment is hard to miss.
talk.armbandEarnMixed: {player} frowns. “I thought I already had. But okay.”
talk.armbandEarnBad: {player} doesn't hide it. “Lead without the armband? That's what I've been doing all season.”
talk.armbandNoGood: {player} accepts it. “Understood. I'll back the captain.”
talk.armbandNoMixed: {player} lets it go, for now. “Okay. The offer stands if you change your mind.”
talk.armbandNoBad: {player} leaves stung. “Right. I know where I stand.” So, before long, does the rest of the room.
talk.positionQ1: {player} has an idea. “I'm getting nowhere at {from_k}, boss. Try me at {to_k}. I've played there before and I think I'd get on the pitch.”
talk.positionQ2: {player} catches you after training. “Every week I watch from the stand. I'm a better {to_k} than you think. Give me a go there.”
talk.positionTrain: Work on it in training first
talk.positionTryGood: {player} is delighted. “Thanks, boss. I'll be ready when the chance comes.”
talk.positionTryMixed: {player} nods. “Great. Let's see if it actually happens.”
talk.positionTryBad: {player} is guarded. “We'll see. I've heard yes before.”
talk.positionTrainGood: {player} likes that. “Makes sense. I'll put the hours in.”
talk.positionTrainMixed: {player} shrugs. “Training's not a match, but okay.”
talk.positionNoGood: {player} takes it well. “Fair enough. I'll keep working at {from_k}.”
talk.positionNoBad: {player} bristles. “Then I'm a {from_k} who doesn't play. That can't go on.”
talk.mateQ1: {player} is at the office door before training. “{mate} and I came through a lot together here, boss. I read about the move on my phone.”
talk.mateQ2: {player} catches you in the car park. “Letting {mate} go? The squad are asking what that says about the rest of us.”
talk.mateSorry: It was a hard call. I know how close the two of you were
talk.mateNeed: I need you to step up and fill that gap now
talk.mateMove: Players come and go. That is the business
talk.mateSorryGood: {player} nods slowly. “Thanks for saying it. That matters more than you'd think.”
talk.mateSorryMixed: {player} shrugs. “A hard call. Right. I'll get on with it.”
talk.mateSorryBad: {player} isn't having it. “If it was that hard, you'd have picked up the phone.”
talk.mateNeedGood: {player} straightens up. “Then I'll do it. Somebody has to keep this group together.”
talk.mateNeedMixed: {player} half nods. “Fine. But don't make a habit of it.”
talk.mateNeedBad: {player} laughs without smiling. “Step up? You've just shown everyone what stepping up gets you.”
talk.mateMoveGood: {player} almost smiles. “Fair enough. It's a job. I'd have done the same.”
talk.mateMoveMixed: {player} looks at the floor. “I suppose it is.” The door closes quietly.
talk.mateMoveBad: {player} walks out. By the afternoon half the squad has heard what you said.

quick.reading: Reads the game with rare maturity, and learns tactical detail quickly.

slow.attack: Handling and passing are slow to come on.

slow.setpiece: Set-piece detail takes longer to sink in than for most.
slow.kicking: The kicking game is slow to improve.

room.depAgainstVice: {deputy}, the vice-captain, has sided with the senior players.
room.depBacksCap: {deputy}, the captain, has told them it was your call to make.
room.depAgainstCap: {deputy}, the captain, has sided with the senior players.
room.depNone: Nobody senior has stepped in to settle it.
room.stand: Stand by it: the side is picked on merit
room.reverse: Reverse it: {player} starts the next match
room.standR: You held the line. {player} is unhappy, and so are the senior players, but the room knows who picks the side. {dep_k}
room.standRLed: You held the line, as this room has come to expect. The senior players grumble, more quietly than they once did. {dep_k}
room.standRPlayers: You held the line, and this room is not used to hearing no. The senior players are angry, and {player} angriest of all. {dep_k}
room.withDeputy: {deputy} stood beside you, at some cost with {player}.
room.withoutDeputy: {deputy} did not stand beside you, and everyone noticed.
room.leftDeputy: {deputy} had backed you in front of the players and has been left exposed.
room.deputyWon: {deputy} got what the senior players asked for.
room.reverseR: {player} starts the next match. The senior players take it as a win; the player who lost the shirt takes it hard. {dep_k}
room.reverseRLed: {player} starts the next match. From a manager who rarely moves, it lands as a gesture, and the room takes it as one. {dep_k}
room.reverseRPlayers: {player} starts the next match. The senior players expected nothing less, and some are already wondering what else they can change. {dep_k}

Wait, and the wage bill stays lighter for now, but from the new year other clubs can agree a pre-contract, and some are already asking.

room.waitLost: {player} has agreed a pre-contract with {to} and will leave on a free this summer. You chose to wait on the renewal; {to} did not.

styles.atk_directDesc: Straight at them: one-out carriers off the ruck, pick-and-go and few passes to drop. Wins the gain line and the penalties that come with it and loses few balls, but makes fewer clean breaks.
styles.atk_podsDesc: A forward on each edge, a pod of three either side of the middle and the backs behind them as the second option. Balanced and hard to read, and the pod shapes among your moves fit it best.
styles.atk_widthDesc: Flat passes to a screen of runners, with the ball swept round the back of them to the outside channels. More line breaks, but a long pass can be picked off and the ruck is left light.
styles.atk_kickDesc: Box kicks and contestable kicks with a chase line under them: territory, the aerial battle and pressure on their back three. Fewer phases and fewer line breaks, and more kicks that can be charged down.
styles.atk_offloadDesc: Keep the ball alive in the tackle and play what is in front of you. The most line breaks of any style, and the most turnovers. It costs legs.
styles.def_driftDesc: Up, then out: the line slides across one man and pushes play towards the touchline, which never misses a tackle. Gives away few penalties.
styles.def_blitzTag: Line speed, no time on the ball
styles.def_blitzDesc: The whole line comes up fast and together, into the carrier before the attack can build speed. Wins the ball behind the gain line, but the offside calls add up, the space in behind is empty and it costs legs.
styles.def_pendulumDesc: A standard line, with the back three swinging behind it to cover the kick space: the ball-side wing up, the full-back deep, the far wing in the middle. Safe, but the line in front is a man short.
styles.def_manDesc: Every defender takes one attacker and stays with that runner. Simple to drill, and how it goes depends on who wins the one-on-ones.
styles.def_chokeTag: Hold them up, win the ball
styles.def_chokeDesc: Tackle high, keep the carrier on their feet and force the maul or the held-up ball. Wins the ball back more than any other defence, but a pack that is stronger at the set piece will drive the maul it invites.
styles.cAtk_direct1: {team} keep coming straight at {opp}, and {def_k} cannot hold the gain line.
styles.cAtk_direct2: Carry after carry from {team}, and every one of them over the gain line.
styles.cAtk_pods1: The pods from {team} ask questions right across the field, and {def_k} has no answer.
styles.cAtk_pods2: One pod after another goes forward, and {team} have {opp} on the back foot.
styles.cAtk_width1: {team} go wide at every chance, and {def_k} cannot get out to the edges.
styles.cAtk_width2: A flat pass, a screen, the sweep round the back: {team} are stretching {opp} to the touchline.
styles.cAtk_kick1: Up and under from {team}, and the chase is on {opp} before the ball comes down. There is nobody behind {def_k}.
styles.cAtk_kick2: {team} kick in behind the rushing line again, and {opp} have to turn and chase.
styles.cAtk_offload1: The ball comes out of the tackle again and {team} are through. {opp} never saw it coming.
styles.cAtk_offload2: {team} keep the ball alive in contact, and the offloads are pulling {def_k} apart.
styles.cDef_drift1: {team} slide across and push {opp} towards the touchline, and {atk_k} runs out of room.
styles.cDef_drift2: The drift is on, and {team} shepherd {opp} into touch.
styles.cDef_blitz1: The blitz from {team} catches {opp} behind the gain line.
styles.cDef_blitz2: {team} fly up off the line and give {opp} no time on the ball.
styles.cDef_pendulum1: The back three are exactly where the kick comes down: {team} have read {atk_k}.
styles.cDef_pendulum2: {opp} kick, and the cover from {team} is already waiting for it.
styles.cDef_man1: Every runner from {opp} has a defender square in front. Man-to-man, and nobody gets free.
styles.cDef_man2: {team} have picked up every runner, and {atk_k} has nowhere to go.
styles.cDef_choke1: Held up! The choke tackle from {team} stops {opp} dead, and the carry goes nowhere.
styles.cDef_choke2: {team} tackle high and hold the ball up, and {atk_k} is playing straight into their hands.
styles.cTurn_drift: {player} reads the pass out wide, and {team} have the turnover.
styles.cTurn_blitz: {player} is up in a flash, and {team} win the ball back.
styles.cTurn_pendulum: {player} sweeps up the loose ball in the cover, and the ball belongs to {team}.
styles.cTurn_man: {player} wins the one-on-one and rips the ball away. Turnover to {team}.
styles.cTurn_choke: Choke tackle! {player} holds the carrier up and {team} win the turnover.

styles.pod_1331Desc: A forward on each edge and two pods of three in the middle: the balanced pod game.
styles.pod_242Desc: Two forwards on each edge and four in the middle: the ball goes wider sooner, with more breaks out wide and a little less go-forward.
styles.pod_nineDesc: One-out runners round the scrum-half: quick ball off short carries, the most gain line and the fewest errors, but fewer breaks.

tt.reactionsSub: every player hears it their own way
tt.pre_calm1: Quiet voice, slow words. You walk the room through the first twenty minutes.
tt.pre_calm2: No theatre. The plan on one whiteboard line, and the pen capped.
tt.pre_faith1: You go round the room and tell each player why the shirt is theirs.
tt.pre_faith2: "I picked this side because I trust it. Go and show them why."
tt.pre_expect1: Standards. You expect a professional performance and nothing less.
tt.pre_expect2: "Win, and win properly." Nothing else needs saying.
tt.pre_fire1: The door rattles on its hinges as the room empties, snorting.
tt.pre_fire2: Two sentences, both loud. The front row are first out of the door.
tt.pre_silent1: Nothing from you again, and the room noticed. Your assistant says so quietly on the way out.
tt.pre_silent2: Another silent dressing room. Your assistant catches your eye: the group was waiting for a word.
tt.ht_calm1: Calm and matter-of-fact. Two fixes on the whiteboard, nothing more.
tt.ht_calm2: You lower the temperature. Trust the system, make the tackle in front of you.
tt.ht_faith1: "Forty minutes. I know what this group has in it." You mean every word.
tt.ht_faith2: You tell them the game is still there to be won, and that you trust them to win it.
tt.ht_praise1: You name three things they did exactly right and ask for more of the same.
tt.ht_praise2: You are delighted with that half, and you tell them so.
tt.ht_demand1: More, you ask. Not different, just more.
tt.ht_demand2: "That was fine. Fine does not win this." You want a better forty.
tt.ht_criticise1: You go through the half one mistake at a time and spare nobody.
tt.ht_criticise2: Out comes the hairdryer. Every error is named, out loud.
tt.ht_fire1: A cup of tea goes flying. Forty minutes of everything, you tell them.
tt.ht_fire2: Voice up, collar loose. The room goes silent, then very loud.
tt.verdict_good: It lands: most of the room looks ready.
tt.verdict_mixed: It lands with some and not with others.
tt.verdict_bad: It misses: the room was in no mood for that.
